Annual Report Due Dates by State (2026 Table) 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILINGS · CORPORATIONS AND LLCS 

# Annual report due dates by state

Most states ask corporations and LLCs to file a short report every year or two to keep their records current, and many dissolve or penalise a business that misses it. The table gives each state's report and when it is due, taken from the state's own page and read on 20 November 2026. Open a state for who files it, the fee and the late penalty where the state states them, with the official wording quoted. 

Organisational guidance, not legal or tax advice. Check the official page before you file. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 
 Due rules as each state words them. Select a state for its sources. 
 State Report and who files When it is due 
 Alabama Alabama Business Privilege Tax return (Form CPT) (c-corporations with a calendar year or a fiscal year other than June 30) Due no later than three and a half months after the start of the taxable year (for example, April 15 for a calendar-year C-corporation). The due date corresponds to the due date of the corresponding federal return. 
 Alabama Business Privilege Tax return (Form CPT) (c-corporations with a June 30 fiscal year) Due no later than two and a half months after the start of the taxable year (for example, September 15 for a June 30 fiscal-year C-corporation). 
 Alabama Business Privilege Tax return (Form PPT)
 Limited liability entities Due no later than two and a half months after the start of the taxable year (for example, March 15 for a calendar-year limited liability entity). 
 Alaska Biennial Report (for-profit corporations, professional corporations, limited liability…) Due by January 2 of every even-numbered year if the entity first filed/registered in an even-numbered year, or of every odd-numbered year if it first filed in an odd-numbered year. The reporting period opens three months before the due date. 
 Biennial Report (nonprofit corporations, cooperatives and religious corporations) Due by July 2 of every even-numbered year if the entity first filed/registered in an even-numbered year, or of every odd-numbered year if it first filed in an odd-numbered year. The reporting period opens three months before the due date. 
 Arizona Annual Report (corporations)
 Corporations (for-profit and nonprofit) Each corporation files by its own designated due date every year; the due date is shown on the corporation's record on the ACC business website. The report can be filed online up to 90 days before it is due. 
 Arkansas Franchise Tax / Annual Report (Arkansas Corporate Franchise Tax Act of 1979)
 Corporations, LLCs, banks and insurance companies registered in Arkansas File on or before May 1 to avoid penalties. 
 California Statement of Information (Statement of Information – CA and Out-of-State Corporation)
 California stock corporations and qualified out-of-state (foreign) corporations Every year, by the last day of the calendar month in which the corporation was originally incorporated or registered. The filing period is a six-month window ending that month (for example, a January registration files between August 1 and January 31). File an updated statement whenever the information changes. 
 Statement of Information (Statement of Information – CA and Out-of-State LLC)
 California LLCs and qualified out-of-state (foreign) LLCs Every two years, in odd or even years matching the year of initial registration, by the last day of the calendar month of registration. The filing period is a six-month window ending that month. File an updated statement whenever the information changes. 
 Colorado Periodic Report
 Reporting entities, including limited liability companies, corporations,… Each entity's 'Periodic report month' is shown on its Summary page in the business database. The report can be filed from two months before that month until two months after it without any penalty. 
 Connecticut Annual report (Limited Liability Company)
 Limited liability companies (LLCs) Due each year between January 1 and March 31 (since 2018; before 2018 LLC reports were due by the last day of the anniversary month). 
 Annual report (Corporation)
 Corporations (stock and nonstock) Due each year by the last day of the anniversary month of formation or registration; can be filed up to one month before the anniversary month. 
 Delaware Annual Report and Franchise Tax (domestic corporations)
 Active domestic (Delaware) corporations On or before March 1 each year, covering the prior year; must be filed online. 
 Annual Report (foreign corporations)
 Foreign corporations registered in Delaware On or before June 30 each year. 
 Annual tax for LLCs, LPs and GPs (no annual report)
 Domestic and foreign LLCs, limited partnerships and general partnerships… Pay the annual tax for the prior year on or before June 1 each year. 
 District of Columbia BRA-25 Two-Year Biennial Report for Domestic and Foreign Filing Entities
 Every domestic and foreign filing entity registered with the DLCP… First report due by April 1 of the calendar year after the entity registers, then by April 1 every two years after that. 
 Florida Annual report (Fla. Stat. § 607.1622)
 Domestic corporations and foreign corporations authorized to transact… Between January 1 and May 1 each year. The first report is due between January 1 and May 1 of the year after the calendar year in which the articles of incorporation became effective or the foreign corporation got its certificate of authority. 
 Annual report (Fla. Stat. § 605.0212)
 Florida LLCs and registered foreign LLCs Between January 1 and May 1 each year. The first report is due between January 1 and May 1 of the year after the calendar year in which the articles of organization became effective or the foreign LLC got its certificate of authority. 
 Georgia Annual Registration
 Each business entity registered or filed with the Georgia Secretary of State… Due by April 1 of each year it is due; can be filed as early as January 1. Registrations may be filed in advance for up to and including 3 calendar years. 
 Hawaii Annual business report (annual report or annual statement)
 Business entities registered with the DCCA Business Registration Division Due by the last day of the calendar quarter in which the entity registered: registered Jan 1–Mar 31, due Mar 31; Apr 1–Jun 30, due Jun 30; Jul 1–Sep 30, due Sep 30; Oct 1–Dec 31, due Dec 31. An entity registered in the same year a report falls due does not file for that year. 
 Kansas Information Report (for-profit businesses on file with the Kansas Secretary of State) Due April 15 every two years: businesses formed in an even year file in each following even year; businesses formed in an odd year file in each following odd year. 
 Information Report (not-for-profit businesses on file with the Kansas Secretary of State) Due June 15 every two years, in even or odd years matching the year of formation. 
 Kentucky Annual Report
 All entities conducting business in Kentucky (domestic and foreign business… File between January 1 and June 30 each year; due by June 30. 
 Maine Annual report
 Legal entities filed with the Maine Secretary of State (domestic and foreign… Due by June 1 each year; file between January 1 and June 1. The first report is due in the calendar year after the entity was incorporated, formed or qualified. 
 Maryland Annual Report (SDAT Form 1 — annual report/personal property return)
 All entities that existed as of January 1 (including LLCs and corporations),… Due by April 15 each year for every entity that existed on January 1. The first filing is due the year after the business is formed (e.g. formed any time in 2024, first Annual Report due by April 15, 2025). 
 Michigan Annual Statement (Limited Liability Companies) / Annual Report and Annual Statement (Professional LLCs)
 Limited liability companies and professional limited liability companies… Due February 15 each year after organization/qualification; an LLC formed or qualified after September 30 does not file on the February 15 immediately following its formation. Online filing opens October 15. 
 Annual Report for Corporations
 Profit corporations and professional corporations (nonprofit corporations… Due May 15 each year after incorporation/qualification; online filing opens January 15. 
 Minnesota Annual renewal
 Most business entities registered in Minnesota By December 31 of each calendar year. The renewal can be filed at any time during the year it is due, and the entity's Business Record Details page shows its next renewal due date. 
 Mississippi Annual Report (for-profit corporations and limited liability companies operating in Mississippi) Can be filed any time on or after January 1 and is due by April 15 of that year. Must be filed online. 
 Annual Report (nonprofit corporations) Can be filed any time on or after January 1 and is due by May 15 of that year. Must be filed online. 
 Missouri Annual registration report
 All corporations doing business in Missouri, domestic and foreign Each year by the end of the month in which the corporation incorporated or qualified (for corporations incorporated or qualified on or after July 1, 2003). A corporation that existed before July 1, 2003 is due at the end of the month shown on its last annual report. The due month cannot be changed. 
 Montana Annual report
 LLCs and corporations (profit and nonprofit) File each year. Reports filed January 1 to April 15 have no fee. Foreign entities must file by November 1 and domestic entities by December 1. 
 Nebraska Biennial occupation tax report
 Domestic and foreign business corporations and professional corporations Due by March 1 of even-numbered years; delinquent April 15. 
 Biennial report
 Domestic and foreign LLCs and professional LLCs Due by April 1 of odd-numbered years; delinquent June 16. 
 Nevada Annual List of Officers, filed together with the State Business License renewal
 Title 7 entities, whose State Business License renewal falls due with the… On the last day of the anniversary month in which the license was originally filed. The Annual List and business license are filed together. The first Initial List and license are due by the last day of the month after formation. 
 New Hampshire Annual Report
 Corporations, professional corporations, benefit corporations, professional… Annual report and filing fee due by April 1 of each year following the year of registration. 
 New Jersey Annual report
 Every business in New Jersey, including LLCs and corporations Due every year by the last day of the month in which the business was formed. 
 New Mexico Corporate Report (Corporate Reports Act, NMSA 1978 § 53-5-2) and supplemental report
 Domestic and foreign corporations that are not exempted (exemptions listed… First report within 30 days after the certificate of incorporation or certificate of authority is issued; then biennially, on or before the 15th day of the fourth month after the end of the corporation's taxable year. A supplemental report is due within 30 days of a change in registered office/agent, directors or officers, or principal place of business. 
 New York Biennial Statement
 Domestic and foreign business corporations (Business Corporation Law § 408)… Every two years, during the calendar month in which the original Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Organization or Application for Authority was filed with the Department of State. Do not file before that month. 
 North Carolina Annual Report (Business Corporations and Banks)
 Business corporations and banks Due the 15th day of the fourth month after the entity's fiscal year ends (April 15 for a calendar-year entity). 
 Annual Report (Limited Liability Companies)
 Limited liability companies (LLC or L3C) Due April 15 of each year after the year the LLC was created. 
 North Dakota Annual Report (domestic business corporations and domestic professional corporations) On or before August 1 each year, starting the year after the year of registration. 
 Annual Report (foreign business corporations and foreign professional corporations) On or before May 15 each year, starting the year after the year of registration. 
 Annual Report (limited liability companies (LLC) and professional limited liability…) On or before November 15 each year, starting the year after the year of registration. 
 Annual Report (farming or ranching LLCs and corporations, and authorized livestock farm…) On or before April 15 each year, starting the year after the year of registration. 
 Annual Report (limited partnerships, limited liability partnerships, limited liability…) On or before March 31 each year, starting the year after the year of registration. 
 Oregon Annual Report or Renewal
 All business entity types except assumed business names (which renew every… Due on the anniversary date of the original filing each year. The Secretary of State sends a renewal notice about 45 days before. 
 Pennsylvania Annual Report [DSCB:15-146] — corporations
 Business and nonprofit corporations, domestic and foreign File between January 1 and June 30 each year (deadline June 30). 
 Annual Report [DSCB:15-146] — limited liability companies
 Limited liability companies, domestic and foreign File between January 1 and September 30 each year (deadline September 30). 
 Rhode Island Annual Report
 Limited liability companies, business corporations, and limited partnerships… File between February 1 and May 1 each year, starting the calendar year after the business registers with the state. 
 Annual Report (domestic benefit corporations, Form 633)
 Domestic benefit corporations Within 120 days of the end of the corporation's fiscal year. 
 South Carolina Annual report (Schedule D of the SC Corporate Tax return)
 Generally every domestic corporation, every foreign corporation qualified to… Due with the corporate tax return, by the return due date: C corporations (SC1120) by April 15 for calendar-year filers, otherwise the 15th day of the 4th month after the tax year ends; S corporations (SC1120S) by March 15, otherwise the 15th day of the 3rd month after the tax year ends. 
 Tennessee Annual report (corporation)
 Corporations Due on or before the first day of the fourth month after the close of the corporation's fiscal year. If no fiscal-year close month was given in the charter, the Division of Business Services records December by default. 
 Texas Annual Franchise Tax Report, plus Public Information Report (Form 05-102) or Ownership Information Report (Form 05-167)
 Each taxable entity formed or organized in Texas or doing business in Texas Due May 15 each year; if May 15 falls on a weekend or holiday, due the next business day. 
 Utah Annual report for division
 Each domestic filing entity and registered foreign entity Each calendar year by the last day of the entity's anniversary month: the month its formation became effective with the Division or, for a foreign entity, the month its authority to conduct affairs in Utah took effect. It may be filed up to 60 days before that date. The Division may set a different period by rule. 
 Vermont Annual Report (profit corporations and profit cooperative corporations) Within the first two and a half months following the fiscal year end on record (renewed each fiscal year). 
 Annual Report (limited liability companies (LLC/PLC/L3C)) Within the first three months following the fiscal year end on record (renewed each fiscal year). 
 Virginia Annual report (Code of Virginia § 13.1-775)
 Domestic corporations and foreign corporations authorized to transact… Each year on or before the last day of the month in which the corporation was incorporated or authorized in Virginia (stated as the last day of the twelfth month after that month, then the same date each year). It can be filed no earlier than three months before the due date. The State Corporation Commission can move a due date by 1 to 11 months. 
 Annual registration fee (Code of Virginia § 13.1-1062), payment only
 Domestic LLCs, protected series, and foreign LLCs and foreign protected… Each year on or before the last day of the month in which the LLC was organized or registered in Virginia (stated as the last day of the twelfth month after that month, then the same date each year). Different dates apply to LLCs created by conversion or domestication. The Commission can move a due date by 1 to 11 months. 
 Washington Annual Report
 All domestic and foreign business entities Due by the last day of the month in which the business was originally formed or registered. It can be filed up to 180 days before that date, and filing early does not change the expiration date. 
 West Virginia Annual Report
 Organizations registered through the West Virginia Secretary of State (most… File between January 1 and June 30 each year, starting the calendar year after the business registered with the Secretary of State. 
 Wisconsin Annual Report (domestic entities)
 Domestic business corporations (Ch Due each year after the calendar year of registration, during the calendar quarter containing the registration anniversary date; due by the last day of that quarter (March 31, June 30, September 30 or December 31). 
 Annual Report (foreign entities)
 Foreign entities registered to transact business in Wisconsin Due during the first calendar quarter (by March 31) of each year after the calendar year in which the foreign entity registered. 
 Wyoming Annual Report
 Corporations, LLCs, LPs, RLLPs and SFs (statutory trusts have their own date) Due on the first day of the anniversary month of the initial filing each year. For example, an entity first filed on May 15 is due May 1 each year. Statutory trust annual reports are due by January 1 each year.

We publish a state only when its official page could be read and quoted. Not covered yet: Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Oklahoma, South Dakota. Check those states' Secretary of State websites directly.

Alabama Annual Report Due Date and Who Files 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · ALABAMA 

# Alabama annual report due date

 Alabama Business Privilege Tax return (Form CPT) (c-corporations with a calendar year or a fiscal year other than June 30) : Due no later than three and a half months after the start of the taxable year (for example, April 15 for a calendar-year C-corporation). The due date corresponds to the due date of the corresponding federal return.
 Alabama Business Privilege Tax return (Form CPT) (c-corporations with a June 30 fiscal year) : Due no later than two and a half months after the start of the taxable year (for example, September 15 for a June 30 fiscal-year C-corporation).
 Alabama Business Privilege Tax return (Form PPT) : Due no later than two and a half months after the start of the taxable year (for example, March 15 for a calendar-year limited liability entity). 

From the official Alabama Department of Revenue page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Alabama Business Privilege Tax return (Form CPT) (c-corporations with a calendar year or a fiscal year other than June 30)

### Who files it

C-corporations with a calendar year or a fiscal year other than June 30. 
The official page says: “For C-corporations with a calendar year or a fiscal year other than June 30” ( Alabama Department of Revenue — When is the Alabama Business Privilege Tax return due? ) 

### When it is due

Due no later than three and a half months after the start of the taxable year (for example, April 15 for a calendar-year C-corporation). The due date corresponds to the due date of the corresponding federal return. 
The official page says: “no later than three and a half months after the beginning of a taxpayer’s” ( Alabama Department of Revenue — When is the Alabama Business Privilege Tax return due? ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

The state's page we read does not state a late penalty. Ask the filing office before the date passes. 

## Alabama Business Privilege Tax return (Form CPT) (c-corporations with a June 30 fiscal year)

### Who files it

C-corporations with a June 30 fiscal year. 
The official page says: “For C-corporations with a fiscal year of June 30” ( Alabama Department of Revenue — When is the Alabama Business Privilege Tax return due? ) 

### When it is due

Due no later than two and a half months after the start of the taxable year (for example, September 15 for a June 30 fiscal-year C-corporation). 
The official page says: “Form CPT would be due on September 15, 2021 for C-corporations” ( Alabama Department of Revenue — When is the Alabama Business Privilege Tax return due? ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

The state's page we read does not state a late penalty. Ask the filing office before the date passes. 

## Alabama Business Privilege Tax return (Form PPT)

### Who files it

Limited liability entities. 
The official page says: “For Limited Liability Entities, the Alabama business privilege tax return is due” ( Alabama Department of Revenue — When is the Alabama Business Privilege Tax return due? ) 

### When it is due

Due no later than two and a half months after the start of the taxable year (for example, March 15 for a calendar-year limited liability entity). 
The official page says: “later than two and a half months after the beginning of the taxpayer’s taxable year” ( Alabama Department of Revenue — When is the Alabama Business Privilege Tax return due? ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

The state's page we read does not state a late penalty. Ask the filing office before the date passes.

Alaska Annual Report Due Date: Biennial Report 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · ALASKA 

# Alaska annual report due date

 Biennial Report (for-profit corporations, professional corporations, limited liability…) : Due by January 2 of every even-numbered year if the entity first filed/registered in an even-numbered year, or of every odd-numbered year if it first filed in an odd-numbered year. The reporting period opens three months before the due date.
 Biennial Report (nonprofit corporations, cooperatives and religious corporations) : Due by July 2 of every even-numbered year if the entity first filed/registered in an even-numbered year, or of every odd-numbered year if it first filed in an odd-numbered year. The reporting period opens three months before the due date. 

From the official Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Biennial Report (for-profit corporations, professional corporations, limited liability…)

### Who files it

For-profit corporations, professional corporations, limited liability companies and limited liability partnerships. 
The official page says: “For Profit Corporations, Professional Corporations, Limited Liability Companies and Limited Liability Partnerships:” ( Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing — Biennial Reports ) 

### When it is due

Due by January 2 of every even-numbered year if the entity first filed/registered in an even-numbered year, or of every odd-numbered year if it first filed in an odd-numbered year. The reporting period opens three months before the due date. It is filed every two years. 
The official page says: “Biennial Reports are due by January 2nd, reports marked after February 1st” ( Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing — Biennial Reports ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

Late fee penalties apply to reports marked after February 1 (amount not stated on the state's page). 
The official page says: “reports marked after February 1st incur late fee penalties” ( Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing — Biennial Reports ) 

File online through the state's filing service . 

## Biennial Report (nonprofit corporations, cooperatives and religious corporations)

### Who files it

Nonprofit corporations, cooperatives and religious corporations. 
The official page says: “Non Profit Corporations, Cooperatives and Religious Corporations:” ( Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing — Biennial Reports ) 

### When it is due

Due by July 2 of every even-numbered year if the entity first filed/registered in an even-numbered year, or of every odd-numbered year if it first filed in an odd-numbered year. The reporting period opens three months before the due date. It is filed every two years. 
The official page says: “Biennial Reports are due by July 2nd, reports post marked after August 1st” ( Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing — Biennial Reports ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

Late fee penalties apply to reports postmarked after August 1 (amount not stated on the state's page). 
The official page says: “reports post marked after August 1st incur late fee penalties” ( Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing — Biennial Reports ) 

File online through the state's filing service .

Arizona Annual Report Due Date, Fee and Late Penalty 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · ARIZONA 

# Arizona annual report due date

 Annual Report (corporations) : Each corporation files by its own designated due date every year; the due date is shown on the corporation's record on the ACC business website. The report can be filed online up to 90 days before it is due. 

From the official Arizona Corporation Commission page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the Arizona Annual Report (corporations)?

Corporations (for-profit and nonprofit). Arizona LLCs are not required to file annual reports. 
The official page says: “Only corporations are required to file annual reports.” ( Arizona Corporation Commission — Business Services FAQs ) 

## When is the Arizona annual report due?

Each corporation files by its own designated due date every year; the due date is shown on the corporation's record on the ACC business website. The report can be filed online up to 90 days before it is due. 
The official page says: “Each corporation must file their annual report by their designated due date each year.” ( Arizona Corporation Commission — Business Services FAQs ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Arizona?

$45 for for-profit corporations; $10 for nonprofit corporations. 
The official page says: “fee of $45 and nonprofit corporations have an annual report filing fee of $10” ( Arizona Corporation Commission — Business Services FAQs ) 

## What happens if the Arizona report is late?

For-profit corporations: $9.00 per month accrues once the deadline is missed. Nonprofit corporations are not assessed penalties. A delinquency notice is sent and status changes to Pending Inactive; about 60 days later a final delinquency notice; about 60 days after that the corporation is administratively dissolved. Reinstatement is possible for six years from dissolution at a cost of $100. 
The official page says: “penalties in the amount of $9.00 per month begin to accrue” ( Arizona Corporation Commission — Business Services FAQs ) 

File online through the state's filing service . 

## Put the date in your calendar

Your own due date depends on when and how your business was formed, so the state page is where you confirm it. Once you know it, the renewal reminder calculator works out the reminder dates and gives you a calendar file.

Arkansas Annual Report Due Date, Fee and Late Penalty 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · ARKANSAS 

# Arkansas annual report due date

 Franchise Tax / Annual Report (Arkansas Corporate Franchise Tax Act of 1979) : File on or before May 1 to avoid penalties. 

From the official Arkansas Secretary of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the Arkansas Franchise Tax / Annual Report (Arkansas Corporate Franchise Tax Act of 1979)?

Corporations, LLCs, banks and insurance companies registered in Arkansas. 
The official page says: “requires all Corporations, LLC's, Banks, and Insurance Companies registered in Arkansas” ( Arkansas Secretary of State — Franchise Tax / Annual Report Forms ) 

## When is the Arkansas annual report due?

File on or before May 1 to avoid penalties. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “Filing due on or before May 1 to avoid penalties” ( Arkansas Secretary of State — State Franchise Tax and Annual Report Filing System ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Arkansas?

Varies by entity type: LLC or PLLC $150; corporations with stock minimum $150; corporations without stock $300; banks minimum $150; online card payments add a processing fee (page states $5.00 for credit card, $3 for electronic check). 
The official page says: “Limited Liability Company LLC or PLLC N/A $150 $150” ( Arkansas Secretary of State — Franchise Tax / Annual Report Forms ) 

## What happens if the Arkansas report is late?

Failure to pay can bring additional fees, penalties and interest, or revocation of the authorization to do business; franchise taxes keep accruing even for revoked businesses; further BCS filings are prohibited for entities that fail to pay. 
The official page says: “or even revocation of the authorization to do business” ( Arkansas Secretary of State — Franchise Tax / Annual Report Forms ) 

File online through the state's filing service .

California Annual Report Due Date, Fee and Late Penalty 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · CALIFORNIA 

# California annual report due date

 Statement of Information (Statement of Information – CA and Out-of-State Corporation) : Every year, by the last day of the calendar month in which the corporation was originally incorporated or registered. The filing period is a six-month window ending that month (for example, a January registration files between August 1 and January 31). File an updated statement whenever the information changes.
 Statement of Information (Statement of Information – CA and Out-of-State LLC) : Every two years, in odd or even years matching the year of initial registration, by the last day of the calendar month of registration. The filing period is a six-month window ending that month. File an updated statement whenever the information changes. 

From the official California Secretary of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Statement of Information (Statement of Information – CA and Out-of-State Corporation)

### Who files it

California stock corporations and qualified out-of-state (foreign) corporations; the FAQ also lists cooperative and credit union corporations as annual filers. 
The official page says: “CA Stock Corporations and Qualified Out-of-State Corporations are required to file” ( California Secretary of State — Business Entities FAQs ) 

### When it is due

Every year, by the last day of the calendar month in which the corporation was originally incorporated or registered. The filing period is a six-month window ending that month (for example, a January registration files between August 1 and January 31). File an updated statement whenever the information changes. 
The official page says: “yearly in the month of registration with the California Secretary of State” ( California Secretary of State — Business Entities FAQs ) 

### What it costs

$20 or $25; the state's page gives both amounts without saying which applies to which entity type. 
The official page says: “The fee for filing a Statement of Information is $20 or $25.” ( California Secretary of State — Business Entities FAQs ) 

### If it is late

The Franchise Tax Board assesses a penalty if the statement is still not filed 60 days after the Secretary of State sends a notice of delinquency; the amount is not stated. The corporation's powers, rights and privileges (including the right to use its name in California) can be suspended or forfeited by the Secretary of State. 
The official page says: “Penalties are assessed by the Franchise Tax Board when a business entity has not filed” ( California Secretary of State — Business Entities FAQs ) 

File online through the state's filing service . 

## Statement of Information (Statement of Information – CA and Out-of-State LLC)

### Who files it

California LLCs and qualified out-of-state (foreign) LLCs. 
The official page says: “all California and qualified out-of-state limited liability companies” ( California Secretary of State — Business Entities FAQs ) 

### When it is due

Every two years, in odd or even years matching the year of initial registration, by the last day of the calendar month of registration. The filing period is a six-month window ending that month. File an updated statement whenever the information changes. 
The official page says: “file every two years in the month of registration in even or odd years” ( California Secretary of State — Business Entities FAQs ) 

### What it costs

$20 or $25; the state's page gives both amounts without saying which applies to which entity type. 
The official page says: “The fee for filing a Statement of Information is $20 or $25.” ( California Secretary of State — Business Entities FAQs ) 

### If it is late

The Franchise Tax Board assesses a penalty if the statement is still not filed 60 days after the Secretary of State sends a notice of delinquency; the amount is not stated. Suspension or forfeiture of the entity, in addition to Franchise Tax Board penalties. 
The official page says: “Penalties are assessed by the Franchise Tax Board when a business entity has not filed” ( California Secretary of State — Business Entities FAQs ) 

File online through the state's filing service . 

## Put the date in your calendar

Your own due date depends on when and how your business was formed, so the state page is where you confirm it. Once you know it, the renewal reminder calculator works out the reminder dates and gives you a calendar file.

Colorado Annual Report Due Date: Periodic Report 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · COLORADO 

# Colorado annual report due date

 Periodic Report : Each entity's 'Periodic report month' is shown on its Summary page in the business database. The report can be filed from two months before that month until two months after it without any penalty. 

From the official Colorado Secretary of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the Colorado Periodic Report?

Reporting entities, including limited liability companies, corporations, nonprofit corporations, foreign entities, cooperatives, limited partnerships formed after July 26, 2009, LLPs and LLLPs. 
The official page says: “Reporting entities, such as limited liability companies, corporations, nonprofit corporations, and foreign entities” ( Colorado Secretary of State — Business FAQs: Periodic reports ) 

## When is the Colorado annual report due?

Each entity's 'Periodic report month' is shown on its Summary page in the business database. The report can be filed from two months before that month until two months after it without any penalty. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “filed two months prior to the Periodic Report month or two months after” ( Colorado Secretary of State — Business FAQs: Periodic reports ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Colorado?

$25.00 (online). 
The official page says: “Periodic Report $25.00 n/a Periodic Report Late Filing Penalty $50.00” ( Colorado Secretary of State — Business Organizations Fee Schedule (linked from the FAQ) ) 

## What happens if the Colorado report is late?

$50.00 Periodic Report late filing penalty. The entity's status becomes 'Delinquent' if the report is not filed. 
The official page says: “Periodic Report Late Filing Penalty $50.00” ( Colorado Secretary of State — Business Organizations Fee Schedule (linked from the FAQ) ) 

File online through the state's filing service .

Connecticut Annual Report Due Date and Late Penalty 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · CONNECTICUT 

# Connecticut annual report due date

 Annual report (Limited Liability Company) : Due each year between January 1 and March 31 (since 2018; before 2018 LLC reports were due by the last day of the anniversary month).
 Annual report (Corporation) : Due each year by the last day of the anniversary month of formation or registration; can be filed up to one month before the anniversary month. 

From the official Connecticut Secretary of the State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Annual report (Limited Liability Company)

### Who files it

Limited liability companies (LLCs). 
The official page says: “Limited Liability Company (LLC) Reports” ( Connecticut Secretary of the State — Annual Report Frequently Asked Questions (PDF) ) 

### When it is due

Due each year between January 1 and March 31 (since 2018; before 2018 LLC reports were due by the last day of the anniversary month). It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “The report is due each year between Jan. 1st and March 31st” ( Connecticut Secretary of the State — Annual Report Frequently Asked Questions (PDF) ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

None. The FAQ answers 'No' to whether there is an additional or penalty fee for filing after the due date. The Secretary will not issue a Certificate of Legal Existence (Good Standing) to an entity behind on annual reports, and may administratively dissolve an entity more than one year in default. 
The official page says: “penalty fee if the report is not filed by its due date? No.” ( Connecticut Secretary of the State — Annual Report Frequently Asked Questions (PDF) ) 

## Annual report (Corporation)

### Who files it

Corporations (stock and nonstock). 
The official page says: “Corporation Annual Reports When is it due?” ( Connecticut Secretary of the State — Annual Report Frequently Asked Questions (PDF) ) 

### When it is due

Due each year by the last day of the anniversary month of formation or registration; can be filed up to one month before the anniversary month. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “Reports are due each year by the last day of the anniversary month of formation” ( Connecticut Secretary of the State — Annual Report Frequently Asked Questions (PDF) ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

The Secretary may administratively dissolve any entity more than one year in default of its annual report filing obligation (stated in the LLC section, which refers to 'any entity'). 
The official page says: “the Secretary may administratively dissolve any entity that is more than one year in default” ( Connecticut Secretary of the State — Annual Report Frequently Asked Questions (PDF) )

Updated: 2026-11-20

Delaware Annual Report Due Date, Fee and Late Penalty 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · DELAWARE 

# Delaware annual report due date

 Annual Report and Franchise Tax (domestic corporations) : On or before March 1 each year, covering the prior year; must be filed online.
 Annual Report (foreign corporations) : On or before June 30 each year.
 Annual tax for LLCs, LPs and GPs (no annual report) : Pay the annual tax for the prior year on or before June 1 each year. 

From the official Delaware Division of Corporations page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Annual Report and Franchise Tax (domestic corporations)

### Who files it

Active domestic (Delaware) corporations. 
The official page says: “All active Domestic Corporation Annual Reports and Franchise Taxes” ( Delaware Division of Corporations — Annual Report and Tax Instructions ) 

### When it is due

On or before March 1 each year, covering the prior year; must be filed online. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “are due annually on or before March 1st and are required to be filed online” ( Delaware Division of Corporations — Annual Report and Tax Instructions ) 

### What it costs

Annual report filing fee: $50 for non-exempt domestic corporations, $25 for exempt domestic corporations (effective September 1, 2019). Franchise tax is extra: minimum $175 (Authorized Shares Method) or $400 (Assumed Par Value Capital Method), maximum $200,000 ($250,000 for Large Corporate Filers). 
The official page says: “Exempt Domestic Corporations – $25.00. Non-Exempt Domestic Corporations – $50.00.” ( Delaware Division of Corporations — Annual Report and Tax Instructions ) 

### If it is late

$200 penalty plus 1.5% interest per month on tax and penalty. 
The official page says: “a penalty of $200.00 plus 1.5% interest per month on tax and penalty” ( Delaware Division of Corporations — Annual Report and Tax Instructions ) 

File online through the state's filing service . 

## Annual Report (foreign corporations)

### Who files it

Foreign corporations registered in Delaware. 
The official page says: “Foreign Corporations must file an Annual Report” ( Delaware Division of Corporations — Annual Report and Tax Instructions ) 

### When it is due

On or before June 30 each year. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “Delaware Secretary of State on or before June 30 each year” ( Delaware Division of Corporations — Annual Report and Tax Instructions ) 

### What it costs

$250 filing fee. 
The official page says: “A $250.00 filing fee is required to be paid.” ( Delaware Division of Corporations — Annual Report and Tax Instructions ) 

### If it is late

$250 penalty added to the filing fee if the report and payment are not received by the due date. 
The official page says: “a $250.00 penalty will be added to filing fee” ( Delaware Division of Corporations — Annual Report and Tax Instructions ) 

File online through the state's filing service . 

## Annual tax for LLCs, LPs and GPs (no annual report)

### Who files it

Domestic and foreign LLCs, limited partnerships and general partnerships formed or registered in Delaware. They file no annual report. 
The official page says: “All Domestic and Foreign Limited Liability Companies, Limited Partnerships, and General Partnerships” ( Delaware Division of Corporations — LLC/LP/GP Franchise Tax Instructions ) 

### When it is due

Pay the annual tax for the prior year on or before June 1 each year. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “The annual taxes for the prior year are due on or before June 1st.” ( Delaware Division of Corporations — LLC/LP/GP Franchise Tax Instructions ) 

### What it costs

$400 annual tax (no proration). 
The official page says: “they must pay the $400 yearly tax on or before June 1st” ( Delaware Division of Corporations — LLC/LP/GP Franchise Tax Instructions ) 

### If it is late

$200 penalty plus 1.5% interest per month on tax and penalty. 
The official page says: “Failure to pay the required annual taxes will result in a penalty of $200.00” ( Delaware Division of Corporations — LLC/LP/GP Franchise Tax Instructions ) 

File online through the state's filing service .

STATE FILING · DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA 

# District of Columbia annual report due date

 BRA-25 Two-Year Biennial Report for Domestic and Foreign Filing Entities : First report due by April 1 of the calendar year after the entity registers, then by April 1 every two years after that. 

From the official DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the District of Columbia BRA-25 Two-Year Biennial Report for Domestic and Foreign Filing Entities?

Every domestic and foreign filing entity registered with the DLCP Corporations Division (e.g., corporations, LLCs, partnerships). 
The official page says: “Every entity registered with Corporations Divisions needs to file periodic BRA-25” ( DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection — Corporations Division Business Registration FAQs ) 

## When is the District of Columbia annual report due?

First report due by April 1 of the calendar year after the entity registers, then by April 1 every two years after that. 
The official page says: “first Biennial Report is due by April 1 st the very next calendar year” ( DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection — Corporations Division Business Registration FAQs ) 

## How much does it cost to file in District of Columbia?

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

## What happens if the District of Columbia report is late?

Filing the biennial report, and keeping a registered agent, is required to stay in active and good standing status; the state's page does not set out a specific penalty. 
The official page says: “in order to stay in active and good standing status” ( DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection — Corporations Division Business Registration FAQs )

Florida Annual Report Due Date and Late Penalty 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · FLORIDA 

# Florida annual report due date

 Annual report (Fla. Stat. § 607.1622) : Between January 1 and May 1 each year. The first report is due between January 1 and May 1 of the year after the calendar year in which the articles of incorporation became effective or the foreign corporation got its certificate of authority.
 Annual report (Fla. Stat. § 605.0212) : Between January 1 and May 1 each year. The first report is due between January 1 and May 1 of the year after the calendar year in which the articles of organization became effective or the foreign LLC got its certificate of authority. 

From the official Florida Senate page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Annual report (Fla. Stat. § 607.1622)

### Who files it

Domestic corporations and foreign corporations authorized to transact business in Florida. 
The official page says: “Each domestic corporation and each foreign corporation authorized to transact business in this state” ( Florida Senate — 2026 Florida Statutes § 607.1622, Annual report for department ) 

### When it is due

Between January 1 and May 1 each year. The first report is due between January 1 and May 1 of the year after the calendar year in which the articles of incorporation became effective or the foreign corporation got its certificate of authority. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “Subsequent annual reports must be delivered to the department between January 1 and May 1” ( Florida Senate — 2026 Florida Statutes § 607.1622, Annual report for department ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

Until the report is filed and all fees and penalties are paid, the corporation cannot bring or maintain a lawsuit in a Florida court, and it can be dissolved or have its certificate of authority cancelled. 
The official page says: “may not prosecute or maintain any action in any court of this state” ( Florida Senate — 2026 Florida Statutes § 607.1622, Annual report for department ) 

## Annual report (Fla. Stat. § 605.0212)

### Who files it

Florida LLCs and registered foreign LLCs. 
The official page says: “A limited liability company or a registered foreign limited liability company” ( Florida Senate — 2026 Florida Statutes § 605.0212, Annual report for department (LLCs) ) 

### When it is due

Between January 1 and May 1 each year. The first report is due between January 1 and May 1 of the year after the calendar year in which the articles of organization became effective or the foreign LLC got its certificate of authority. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “Subsequent annual reports must be delivered to the department between January 1 and May 1” ( Florida Senate — 2026 Florida Statutes § 607.1622, Annual report for department ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

Until the report is filed and all fees and penalties are paid, the LLC cannot maintain or defend a lawsuit in a Florida court, and it can be dissolved or have its certificate of authority cancelled. 
The official page says: “may not maintain or defend any action in a court of this state” ( Florida Senate — 2026 Florida Statutes § 605.0212, Annual report for department (LLCs) )

Georgia Annual Report Due Date: Annual Registration 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · GEORGIA 

# Georgia annual report due date

 Annual Registration : Due by April 1 of each year it is due; can be filed as early as January 1. Registrations may be filed in advance for up to and including 3 calendar years. 

From the official Georgia Secretary of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the Georgia Annual Registration?

Each business entity registered or filed with the Georgia Secretary of State (corporations including profit, nonprofit and professional; LLCs; LPs, LLPs and LLLPs). 
The official page says: “Each business entity registered or filed with the Office of Secretary of State” ( Georgia Secretary of State — How to Guide: File Annual Registration ) 

## When is the Georgia annual report due?

Due by April 1 of each year it is due; can be filed as early as January 1. Registrations may be filed in advance for up to and including 3 calendar years. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “Entity annual registrations are due by April 1st of each year it is due” ( Georgia Secretary of State — How to Guide: File Annual Registration ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Georgia?

$60 (profit corp., professional corp., benefit corp., LLC, LP, LLLP, trust estate); $40 (nonprofit corporation); $35 (foreign LLP); same online or paper. 
The official page says: “Annual Registration (Profit Corp., Professional Corp., Benefit Corp., LLC, LP, LLLP, Trust Estate) | $60.00” ( Georgia Secretary of State — How to Guide: File Annual Registration ) 

## What happens if the Georgia report is late?

$25 penalty for late filing. Entities that do not timely file, with all required fees, may be administratively dissolved or have their authorization to transact business in Georgia revoked. 
The official page says: “Penalty for Late Filing of Annual Registration | $25.00” ( Georgia Secretary of State — How to Guide: File Annual Registration )

# Hawaii annual report due date

 Annual business report (annual report or annual statement) : Due by the last day of the calendar quarter in which the entity registered: registered Jan 1–Mar 31, due Mar 31; Apr 1–Jun 30, due Jun 30; Jul 1–Sep 30, due Sep 30; Oct 1–Dec 31, due Dec 31. An entity registered in the same year a report falls due does not file for that year. 

From the official Hawaii DCCA Business Registration Division page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the Hawaii Annual business report (annual report or annual statement)?

Business entities registered with the DCCA Business Registration Division.

## When is the Hawaii annual report due?

Due by the last day of the calendar quarter in which the entity registered: registered Jan 1–Mar 31, due Mar 31; Apr 1–Jun 30, due Jun 30; Jul 1–Sep 30, due Sep 30; Oct 1–Dec 31, due Dec 31. An entity registered in the same year a report falls due does not file for that year. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “January 1 and March 31, the annual report or statement is due by March 31” ( Hawaii DCCA Business Registration Division — BREG Frequently Asked Questions ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Hawaii?

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

## What happens if the Hawaii report is late?

The state's page we read does not state a late penalty. Ask the filing office before the date passes.

Updated: 2026-11-20

Kansas Annual Report Due Date: Information Report 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · KANSAS 

# Kansas annual report due date

 Information Report (for-profit businesses on file with the Kansas Secretary of State) : Due April 15 every two years: businesses formed in an even year file in each following even year; businesses formed in an odd year file in each following odd year.
 Information Report (not-for-profit businesses on file with the Kansas Secretary of State) : Due June 15 every two years, in even or odd years matching the year of formation. 

From the official Kansas Secretary of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Information Report (for-profit businesses on file with the Kansas Secretary of State)

### Who files it

For-profit businesses on file with the Kansas Secretary of State. 
The official page says: “submitted every two years by any business on file with the Kansas Secretary of State” ( Kansas Secretary of State — Information Reports ) 

### When it is due

Due April 15 every two years: businesses formed in an even year file in each following even year; businesses formed in an odd year file in each following odd year. 
The official page says: “for profit businesses are due by April 15th of their respective odd or even year” ( Kansas Secretary of State — Information Reports ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

A three-month delinquency period after the due date, when the report can still be filed but the business is limited in what documents it can file. No dollar penalty is stated. If the three-month delinquency period passes, the business forfeits and cannot file any other document until it submits past-due reports and is reinstated. 
The official page says: “This is a three-month interval after the due date” ( Kansas Secretary of State — Information Reports ) 

## Information Report (not-for-profit businesses on file with the Kansas Secretary of State)

### Who files it

Not-for-profit businesses on file with the Kansas Secretary of State. 
The official page says: “all not for profit businesses are due by June 15th” ( Kansas Secretary of State — Information Reports ) 

### When it is due

Due June 15 every two years, in even or odd years matching the year of formation. 
The official page says: “all not for profit businesses are due by June 15th of their respective” ( Kansas Secretary of State — Information Reports ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

A three-month delinquency period after the due date, when the report can still be filed but the business is limited in what documents it can file. No dollar penalty is stated. If the three-month delinquency period passes, the business forfeits and cannot file any other document until it submits past-due reports and is reinstated. 
The official page says: “This is a three-month interval after the due date” ( Kansas Secretary of State — Information Reports )

STATE FILING · KENTUCKY 

# Kentucky annual report due date

 Annual Report : File between January 1 and June 30 each year; due by June 30. 

From the official Kentucky Secretary of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the Kentucky Annual Report?

All entities conducting business in Kentucky (domestic and foreign business entities). 
The official page says: “all entities conducting business in the Commonwealth of Kentucky” ( Kentucky Secretary of State — Annual Reports ) 

## When is the Kentucky annual report due?

File between January 1 and June 30 each year; due by June 30. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “Reports can be filed any time between January 1 and June 30” ( Kentucky Secretary of State — Annual Reports ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Kentucky?

$15 filing fee. 
The official page says: “accompanied by a $15 filing fee” ( Kentucky Secretary of State — Annual Reports ) 

## What happens if the Kentucky report is late?

Domestic entities that miss June 30 are administratively dissolved (inactive and in bad standing until they reinstate); foreign entities that do not file on time have their certificates of authority revoked. 
The official page says: “Domestic entities that fail to file their annual reports by June 30 are administratively dissolved” ( Kentucky Secretary of State — Annual Reports )

STATE FILING · MAINE 

# Maine annual report due date

 Annual report : Due by June 1 each year; file between January 1 and June 1. The first report is due in the calendar year after the entity was incorporated, formed or qualified. 

From the official Maine Secretary of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the Maine Annual report?

Legal entities filed with the Maine Secretary of State (domestic and foreign business entities and nonprofit corporations). 
The official page says: “your legal entity has been accepted for filing by the Secretary of State's office” ( Maine Secretary of State — Filing Requirement Reminders ) 

## When is the Maine annual report due?

Due by June 1 each year; file between January 1 and June 1. The first report is due in the calendar year after the entity was incorporated, formed or qualified. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “The first annual report filing must be filed between January 1st and June 1st” ( Maine Secretary of State — Filing Requirement Reminders ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Maine?

$85 for domestic business entities; $150 for foreign business entities ($35 for domestic and foreign nonprofit corporations). 
The official page says: “fee is $85 for domestic business entities, $150 for foreign business entities” ( Maine Secretary of State — Filing Requirement Reminders ) 

## What happens if the Maine report is late?

A late filing penalty is assessed if the report is not received by the deadline (amount not stated). Not paying the late filing penalty results in administrative dissolution or revocation of the entity. 
The official page says: “there will be a late filing penalty assessed” ( Maine Secretary of State — Filing Requirement Reminders ) 

File online through the state's filing service .

Maryland Annual Report Due Date and Late Penalty 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · MARYLAND 

# Maryland annual report due date

 Annual Report (SDAT Form 1 — annual report/personal property return) : Due by April 15 each year for every entity that existed on January 1. The first filing is due the year after the business is formed (e.g. formed any time in 2024, first Annual Report due by April 15, 2025). 

From the official Maryland Business Express page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the Maryland Annual Report (SDAT Form 1 — annual report/personal property return)?

All entities that existed as of January 1 (including LLCs and corporations), whether or not they own property or did business. 
The official page says: “All entities are required to file a Form 1” ( Maryland Business Express — Business FAQ (same site) ) 

## When is the Maryland annual report due?

Due by April 15 each year for every entity that existed on January 1. The first filing is due the year after the business is formed (e.g. formed any time in 2024, first Annual Report due by April 15, 2025). It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “by April 15th if they existed as of January 1st.” ( Maryland Business Express — Business FAQ (same site) ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Maryland?

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

## What happens if the Maryland report is late?

A late filing penalty applies to a late Form 1 (amount not stated on the state's page). A business not in Good Standing that does not fix it is forfeited; a forfeited business cannot legally operate in Maryland. Causes of forfeiture include failing to file a previous-year Form 1 (domestic) or current-year Form 1 (foreign), or not paying a late filing penalty. 
The official page says: “pay an outstanding late filing penalty resulting from the late filing of a Form 1” ( Maryland Business Express — Business FAQ (same site) ) 

File online through the state's filing service .

Michigan Annual Report Due Date, Fee and Late Penalty 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · MICHIGAN 

# Michigan annual report due date

 Annual Statement (Limited Liability Companies) / Annual Report and Annual Statement (Professional LLCs) : Due February 15 each year after organization/qualification; an LLC formed or qualified after September 30 does not file on the February 15 immediately following its formation. Online filing opens October 15.
 Annual Report for Corporations : Due May 15 each year after incorporation/qualification; online filing opens January 15. 

From the official Michigan LARA Corporations Division page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Annual Statement (Limited Liability Companies) / Annual Report and Annual Statement (Professional LLCs)

### Who files it

Limited liability companies and professional limited liability companies registered with the Corporations Division. 
The official page says: “LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANIES and PROFESSIONAL LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANIES” ( Michigan LARA Corporations Division — Annual Reports and Annual Statements ) 

### When it is due

Due February 15 each year after organization/qualification; an LLC formed or qualified after September 30 does not file on the February 15 immediately following its formation. Online filing opens October 15. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “Due Date: February 15 each year after organization/qualification.” ( Michigan LARA Corporations Division — Annual Reports and Annual Statements ) 

### What it costs

LLC $25.00; PLLC $75.00. 
The official page says: “LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANIES Fee: $25.00” ( Michigan LARA Corporations Division — Annual Reports and Annual Statements ) 

### If it is late

PLLC: $50.00 penalty fee if received after February 15 (no LLC late penalty stated). Not filing leads to dissolution, revocation or not-good-standing status after a two-year grace period. 
The official page says: “Penalty fee of $50.00 if received after the February 15 due date.” ( Michigan LARA Corporations Division — Annual Reports and Annual Statements ) 

File online through the state's filing service . 

## Annual Report for Corporations

### Who files it

Profit corporations and professional corporations (nonprofit corporations also file, by October 1, $20 fee). 
The official page says: “PROFIT CORPORATIONS and PROFESSIONAL CORPORATIONS” ( Michigan LARA Corporations Division — Annual Reports and Annual Statements ) 

### When it is due

Due May 15 each year after incorporation/qualification; online filing opens January 15. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “Due Date: May 15 each year after incorporation/qualification.” ( Michigan LARA Corporations Division — Annual Reports and Annual Statements ) 

### What it costs

Corporations $25.00 (nonprofit corporations $20.00). 
The official page says: “CORPORATIONS Fee: $25.00 Penalties are imposed if reports” ( Michigan LARA Corporations Division — Annual Reports and Annual Statements ) 

### If it is late

Late penalty rises with lateness: May 16-31 $10; June $20; July $30; August $40; September 1 or later $50. Not filing leads to dissolution, revocation or not-good-standing status after a two-year grace period, or one year for foreign corporations. 
The official page says: “Penalties are imposed if reports are not received by the May 15 due date.” ( Michigan LARA Corporations Division — Annual Reports and Annual Statements ) 

File online through the state's filing service .

Your own due date depends on when and how your business was formed, so the state page is where you confirm it. Once you know it, the renewal reminder calculator works out the reminder dates and gives you a calendar file.

Minnesota Annual Report Due Date: Annual renewal 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · MINNESOTA 

# Minnesota annual report due date

 Annual renewal : By December 31 of each calendar year. The renewal can be filed at any time during the year it is due, and the entity's Business Record Details page shows its next renewal due date. 

From the official Minnesota Secretary of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the Minnesota Annual renewal?

Most business entities registered in Minnesota; the state's page does not list the entity types. 
The official page says: “Most entities need to be renewed yearly to stay active in Minnesota.” ( Minnesota Secretary of State — Renewals (Renewing your Business) ) 

## When is the Minnesota annual report due?

By December 31 of each calendar year. The renewal can be filed at any time during the year it is due, and the entity's Business Record Details page shows its next renewal due date. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “The deadline for renewals is December 31, but you can renew at any time” ( Minnesota Secretary of State — Renewals (Renewing your Business) ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Minnesota?

Free for most entity types; reinstating after a missed renewal requires a fee. 
The official page says: “annual renewals are free (for most entity types), while there is a fee to reinstate” ( Minnesota Secretary of State — Renewals (Renewing your Business) ) 

## What happens if the Minnesota report is late?

The business is administratively dissolved, meaning no longer active in Minnesota, and must be reinstated by filing a current renewal and paying a fee. Its name is reserved for one year after dissolution. 
The official page says: “If you miss the renewal, your business will be administratively dissolved” ( Minnesota Secretary of State — Renewals (Renewing your Business) ) 

File online through the state's filing service .

Missouri Annual Report Due Date: Annual registration report 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · MISSOURI 

# Missouri annual report due date

 Annual registration report : Each year by the end of the month in which the corporation incorporated or qualified (for corporations incorporated or qualified on or after July 1, 2003). A corporation that existed before July 1, 2003 is due at the end of the month shown on its last annual report. The due month cannot be changed. 

From the official Missouri Secretary of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the Missouri Annual registration report?

All corporations doing business in Missouri, domestic and foreign. 
The official page says: “All corporations doing business in this state must file an annual registration report.” ( Missouri Secretary of State — Other Filings Required of General Business Corporations ) 

## When is the Missouri annual report due?

Each year by the end of the month in which the corporation incorporated or qualified (for corporations incorporated or qualified on or after July 1, 2003). A corporation that existed before July 1, 2003 is due at the end of the month shown on its last annual report. The due month cannot be changed. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “annual report is due at the end of the month that the corporation incorporated” ( Missouri Secretary of State — Other Filings Required of General Business Corporations ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Missouri?

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

## What happens if the Missouri report is late?

An extra $15 for each 30-day period the report is late. Administrative dissolution of a domestic corporation's charter, or revocation of a foreign corporation's certificate of authority. The Secretary of State first mails written notice, and the corporation has 60 days to correct or explain. 
The official page says: “Late reports are subject to an additional fee of $15 for each 30-day period.” ( Missouri Secretary of State — Other Filings Required of General Business Corporations ) 

File online through the state's filing service .

Nevada Annual Report Due Date, Fee and Late Penalty 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · NEVADA 

# Nevada annual report due date

 Annual List of Officers, filed together with the State Business License renewal : On the last day of the anniversary month in which the license was originally filed. The Annual List and business license are filed together. The first Initial List and license are due by the last day of the month after formation. 

From the official Nevada Secretary of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the Nevada Annual List of Officers, filed together with the State Business License renewal?

Title 7 entities, whose State Business License renewal falls due with the Annual List of Officers (the state's page does not list which entity types are Title 7). Sole proprietors and partnerships renew the license by the expiration date on it instead. 
The official page says: “For Title 7 entities, the renewal date coincides with the due date” ( Nevada Secretary of State — State Business License - FAQ ) 

## When is the Nevada annual report due?

On the last day of the anniversary month in which the license was originally filed. The Annual List and business license are filed together. The first Initial List and license are due by the last day of the month after formation. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “on the last day of the anniversary month in which the license was originally filed” ( Nevada Secretary of State — State Business License - FAQ ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Nevada?

State Business License renewal: $500 for corporations, $200 for all other entity types. The Annual List of Officers fee is not stated on the state's page. 
The official page says: “$500 for Corporations, and $200 for all other business entity types” ( Nevada Secretary of State — State Business License - FAQ ) 

## What happens if the Nevada report is late?

$100 penalty in addition to the annual business license fee if not paid by the due date. The entity goes into default. After one year in default it is revoked, and reinstatement requires paying all back fees and penalties, including the business license fee. 
The official page says: “shall pay a penalty in the amount of $100 in addition to the annual fee” ( Nevada Secretary of State — State Business License - FAQ ) 

File online through the state's filing service .

STATE FILING · NEW HAMPSHIRE 

# New Hampshire annual report due date

 Annual Report : Annual report and filing fee due by April 1 of each year following the year of registration. 

From the official New Hampshire Secretary of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the New Hampshire Annual Report?

Corporations, professional corporations, benefit corporations, professional benefit corporations, LLCs, professional LLCs, consumer cooperatives and business trusts. 
The official page says: “Corporation, Professional Corporation, *Benefit Corporation, *Professional Benefit Corporation, Limited Liability Company, Professional Limited Liability Company” ( New Hampshire Secretary of State — Business FAQs ) 

## When is the New Hampshire annual report due?

Annual report and filing fee due by April 1 of each year following the year of registration. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “due by April 1st of each year following the year of registration” ( New Hampshire Secretary of State — Business FAQs ) 

## How much does it cost to file in New Hampshire?

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

## What happens if the New Hampshire report is late?

$50 late fee for reports and fees received after April 1; the late fee cannot be waived. Not filed and paid by April 1: status becomes 'Not in Good Standing'. Domestic businesses are administratively dissolved after failing to file for two consecutive years; foreign businesses are administratively suspended after failing to file the current year's report or fee. 
The official page says: “a late fee of $50.00 will be assessed for reports and fees” ( New Hampshire Secretary of State — Business FAQs ) 

File online through the state's filing service . 

## Put the date in your calendar

Your own due date depends on when and how your business was formed, so the state page is where you confirm it. Once you know it, the renewal reminder calculator works out the reminder dates and gives you a calendar file. 

Obligio keeps dates like this on your phone with reminders 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before. It is free for your first three obligations: download on the App Store or get it on Google Play .

Every business in New Jersey, including LLCs and corporations.

New Mexico Annual Report Due Date and Late Penalty 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · NEW MEXICO 

# New Mexico annual report due date

 Corporate Report (Corporate Reports Act, NMSA 1978 § 53-5-2) and supplemental report : First report within 30 days after the certificate of incorporation or certificate of authority is issued; then biennially, on or before the 15th day of the fourth month after the end of the corporation's taxable year. A supplemental report is due within 30 days of a change in registered office/agent, directors or officers, or principal place of business. 

From the official NMOneSource (NM Compilation Commission) page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the New Mexico Corporate Report (Corporate Reports Act, NMSA 1978 § 53-5-2) and supplemental report?

Domestic and foreign corporations that are not exempted (exemptions listed in § 53-5-4). 
The official page says: “a domestic or foreign corporation that is not exempted shall file” ( NMOneSource (NM Compilation Commission) — NMSA 1978 Chapter 53 Corporations, Article 5 Corporate Reports (full-chapter document) ) 

## When is the New Mexico annual report due?

First report within 30 days after the certificate of incorporation or certificate of authority is issued; then biennially, on or before the 15th day of the fourth month after the end of the corporation's taxable year. A supplemental report is due within 30 days of a change in registered office/agent, directors or officers, or principal place of business. It is filed every two years. 
The official page says: “biennially thereafter on or before the fifteenth day of the fourth month” ( NMOneSource (NM Compilation Commission) — NMSA 1978 Chapter 53 Corporations, Article 5 Corporate Reports (full-chapter document) ) 

## How much does it cost to file in New Mexico?

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

## What happens if the New Mexico report is late?

$200 civil penalty for a late report, in addition to the filing fee, payable when the report is filed (§ 53-5-7). Sixty days after written notice of failure to file is mailed, a domestic corporation's certificate of incorporation (or a foreign corporation's certificate of authority) is cancelled unless the report is filed and all fees and penalties are paid in that period; cancelled corporations are stricken from the files. 
The official page says: “shall incur a civil penalty of two hundred dollars ($200)” ( NMOneSource (NM Compilation Commission) — NMSA 1978 Chapter 53 Corporations, Article 5 Corporate Reports (full-chapter document) )

New York Annual Report Due Date: Biennial Statement 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · NEW YORK 

# New York annual report due date

 Biennial Statement : Every two years, during the calendar month in which the original Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Organization or Application for Authority was filed with the Department of State. Do not file before that month. 

From the official New York Department of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the New York Biennial Statement?

Domestic and foreign business corporations (Business Corporation Law § 408) and domestic and foreign LLCs (LLC Law § 301(e)). 
The official page says: “Domestic and foreign business corporations are required by Section 408 of the Business Corporation Law” ( New York Department of State — Biennial Statements for Business Corporations and Limited Liability Companies ) 

## When is the New York annual report due?

Every two years, during the calendar month in which the original Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Organization or Application for Authority was filed with the Department of State. Do not file before that month. 
The official page says: “The filing period for a business corporation or LLC is the calendar month” ( New York Department of State — Biennial Statements for Business Corporations and Limited Liability Companies ) 

## How much does it cost to file in New York?

$9 for a business corporation or LLC. 
The official page says: “The fee for filing a Biennial Statement for a business corporation or LLC is $9.” ( New York Department of State — Biennial Statements for Business Corporations and Limited Liability Companies ) 

## What happens if the New York report is late?

Certificates of Status and status letters will show the entity as past due, which may stop it completing certain business transactions. 
The official page says: “This may prevent the corporation or LLC from completing certain business transactions.” ( New York Department of State — Biennial Statements for Business Corporations and Limited Liability Companies ) 

File online through the state's filing service .
