STATE FILING · NORTH DAKOTA 

# North Dakota annual report due date

 Annual Report (domestic business corporations and domestic professional corporations) : On or before August 1 each year, starting the year after the year of registration.
 Annual Report (foreign business corporations and foreign professional corporations) : On or before May 15 each year, starting the year after the year of registration.
 Annual Report (limited liability companies (LLC) and professional limited liability…) : On or before November 15 each year, starting the year after the year of registration.
 Annual Report (farming or ranching LLCs and corporations, and authorized livestock farm…) : On or before April 15 each year, starting the year after the year of registration.
 Annual Report (limited partnerships, limited liability partnerships, limited liability…) : On or before March 31 each year, starting the year after the year of registration. 

From the official North Dakota Secretary of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Annual Report (domestic business corporations and domestic professional corporations)

### Who files it

Domestic business corporations and domestic professional corporations. 
The official page says: “August 1 Business Corporation (Domestic) Professional Corporation (Domestic)” ( North Dakota Secretary of State — Maintain Registration ) 

### When it is due

On or before August 1 each year, starting the year after the year of registration. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “August 1 Business Corporation (Domestic) Professional Corporation (Domestic)” ( North Dakota Secretary of State — Maintain Registration ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

A late filing fee applies if the report is not received on or before the deadline. The amount is not stated on the state's page. The business is placed in Not Good Standing. Typically it is involuntarily terminated if the past-due report is not filed within 6 to 12 months (a foreign business has its authority revoked). The state's page also says that if the report is not filed within 1 year the business will be involuntarily dissolved or terminated. 
The official page says: “on or before the deadline or incur a late filing fee” ( North Dakota Secretary of State — Maintain Registration ) 

File online through the state's filing service .

Pennsylvania Annual Report Due Date, Fee and Late Penalty 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · PENNSYLVANIA 

# Pennsylvania annual report due date

 Annual Report [DSCB:15-146] — corporations : File between January 1 and June 30 each year (deadline June 30).
 Annual Report [DSCB:15-146] — limited liability companies : File between January 1 and September 30 each year (deadline September 30). 

From the official Pennsylvania Department of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Annual Report [DSCB:15-146] — corporations

### Who files it

Business and nonprofit corporations, domestic and foreign. 
The official page says: “For all corporations (business and nonprofit, domestic and foreign), the deadline is June 30” ( Pennsylvania Department of State — Annual Reports ) 

### When it is due

File between January 1 and June 30 each year (deadline June 30). It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “the deadline is June 30 of each year” ( Pennsylvania Department of State — Annual Reports ) 

### What it costs

$7 for business corporations; $0 for nonprofit corporations. 
The official page says: “The fee is $7 for business corporations, limited liability companies (LLCs)” ( Pennsylvania Department of State — Annual Reports ) 

### If it is late

Starting with reports due in 2027, an association that fails to file is subject to administrative dissolution/termination/cancellation six months after the due date, and loses protection of its name. 
The official page says: “subject to administrative dissolution/termination/cancellation six months after the due date” ( Pennsylvania Department of State — Annual Reports ) 

File online through the state's filing service . 

## Annual Report [DSCB:15-146] — limited liability companies

### Who files it

Limited liability companies, domestic and foreign. 
The official page says: “The deadline for limited liability companies (domestic and foreign) is September 30” ( Pennsylvania Department of State — Annual Reports ) 

### When it is due

File between January 1 and September 30 each year (deadline September 30). It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “Limited liability companies domestic and foreign - Jan. 1 - Sept. 30” ( Pennsylvania Department of State — Annual Reports ) 

### What it costs

$7 for LLCs; $0 for LLCs with a not-for-profit purpose. 
The official page says: “The fee is $7 for business corporations, limited liability companies (LLCs)” ( Pennsylvania Department of State — Annual Reports ) 

### If it is late

Starting with reports due in 2027, an association that fails to file is subject to administrative dissolution/termination/cancellation six months after the due date, and loses protection of its name. 
The official page says: “subject to administrative dissolution/termination/cancellation six months after the due date” ( Pennsylvania Department of State — Annual Reports ) 

File online through the state's filing service .

South Carolina Annual Report Due Date, Fee and Late Penalty 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · SOUTH CAROLINA 

# South Carolina annual report due date

 Annual report (Schedule D of the SC Corporate Tax return) : Due with the corporate tax return, by the return due date: C corporations (SC1120) by April 15 for calendar-year filers, otherwise the 15th day of the 4th month after the tax year ends; S corporations (SC1120S) by March 15, otherwise the 15th day of the 3rd month after the tax year ends. 

From the official South Carolina Department of Revenue page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the South Carolina Annual report (Schedule D of the SC Corporate Tax return)?

Generally every domestic corporation, every foreign corporation qualified to do business in South Carolina, and any other corporation required to file an SC income tax return. Excluded: LLCs not taxed as corporations, corporations whose only SC contact is Secretary of State registration, tax-exempt nonprofits, banks, savings and loans, insurance companies and certain other bodies. Dormant corporations must still file. 
The official page says: “every domestic corporation, every foreign corporation qualified to do business in South Carolina” ( South Carolina Department of Revenue — Corporate FAQs ) 

## When is the South Carolina annual report due?

Due with the corporate tax return, by the return due date: C corporations (SC1120) by April 15 for calendar-year filers, otherwise the 15th day of the 4th month after the tax year ends; S corporations (SC1120S) by March 15, otherwise the 15th day of the 3rd month after the tax year ends. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “License Fee due each year by the due date of your return” ( South Carolina Department of Revenue — Corporate FAQs ) 

## How much does it cost to file in South Carolina?

License Fee: 0.1% of capital stock and paid-in surplus plus $15, minimum $25 (corporations subject to the annual report). 
The official page says: “License Fee rate is 0.1% of the corporation's capital stock and paid-in surplus plus $15.” ( South Carolina Department of Revenue — Corporate FAQs ) 

## What happens if the South Carolina report is late?

Late return: 5% of the unpaid tax per month, up to 25%. Late payment: 0.5% of the tax per month, up to 25%. 
The official page says: “may be penalized 5% of the unpaid tax for each month the return is late” ( South Carolina Department of Revenue — Corporate FAQs ) 

File online through the state's filing service .

Your own due date depends on when and how your business was formed, so the state page is where you confirm it. Once you know it, the renewal reminder calculator works out the reminder dates and gives you a calendar file. 

Obligio keeps dates like this on your phone with reminders 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before. It is free for your first three obligations: download on the App Store or get it on Google Play .

STATE FILING · TENNESSEE 

# Tennessee annual report due date

 Annual report (corporation) : Due on or before the first day of the fourth month after the close of the corporation's fiscal year. If no fiscal-year close month was given in the charter, the Division of Business Services records December by default. 

 This page covers corporations. The Tennessee pages we read do not state when an LLC's annual report is due; check with the Secretary of State. 

From the official Tennessee Secretary of State page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the Tennessee Annual report (corporation)?

Corporations. 
The official page says: “requires corporations to file an annual report with the Secretary of State” ( Tennessee Secretary of State — Instructions, Charter For-Profit Corporation (SS-4417) ) 

## When is the Tennessee annual report due?

Due on or before the first day of the fourth month after the close of the corporation's fiscal year. If no fiscal-year close month was given in the charter, the Division of Business Services records December by default. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “on or before the first day of the fourth month following the end” ( Tennessee Secretary of State — Instructions, Charter For-Profit Corporation (SS-4417) ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Tennessee?

$20, plus $20 more if the registered agent or registered office changes. 
The official page says: “The annual report fee for a corporation is $20” ( Tennessee Secretary of State — Business Services FAQs ) 

## What happens if the Tennessee report is late?

A business entity that does not file its annual report on time may be administratively dissolved and placed in inactive status. 
The official page says: “failed to file its annual report on a timely basis may be administratively dissolved” ( Tennessee Secretary of State — Business Services FAQs )

Texas Annual Report Due Date and Late Penalty 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · TEXAS 

# Texas annual report due date

 Annual Franchise Tax Report, plus Public Information Report (Form 05-102) or Ownership Information Report (Form 05-167) : Due May 15 each year; if May 15 falls on a weekend or holiday, due the next business day. 

From the official Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the Texas Annual Franchise Tax Report, plus Public Information Report (Form 05-102) or Ownership Information Report (Form 05-167)?

Each taxable entity formed or organized in Texas or doing business in Texas. For report year 2024 and later, entities at or below the No Tax Due Threshold do not file a No Tax Due Report but must file a Public Information Report or Ownership Information Report (qualifying new veteran-owned businesses are exempt from both for their first five years). 
The official page says: “imposed on each taxable entity formed or organized in Texas or doing business in Texas” ( Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts — Franchise Tax ) 

## When is the Texas annual report due?

Due May 15 each year; if May 15 falls on a weekend or holiday, due the next business day. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “falls on a weekend or holiday, the due date will be the next business day.” ( Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts — Franchise Tax ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Texas?

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

## What happens if the Texas report is late?

$50 penalty on each report filed after the due date; 5% penalty if tax is paid 1-30 days late, 10% if paid more than 30 days late; interest on past-due tax starts 61 days after the due date. Entities that fail to meet franchise tax filing requirements may receive Form 05-211, Texas Notice of Intent to Forfeit Right to Transact Business, or Form 05-213, Texas Notice of Forfeiture of Registration. 
The official page says: “A $50 penalty is assessed on each report filed after the due date.” ( Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts — Franchise Tax ) 

File online through the state's filing service .

Utah Annual Report Due Date and Who Files 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · UTAH 

# Utah annual report due date

 Annual report for division : Each calendar year by the last day of the entity's anniversary month: the month its formation became effective with the Division or, for a foreign entity, the month its authority to conduct affairs in Utah took effect. It may be filed up to 60 days before that date. The Division may set a different period by rule. 

From the official Utah Legislature page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Who has to file the Utah Annual report for division?

Each domestic filing entity and registered foreign entity. The statute does not name entity types such as corporations or LLCs. 
The official page says: “Each domestic filing entity and registered foreign entity shall file an annual report” ( Utah Legislature — Utah Code § 16-1a-212, Annual report for division (Effective 10/1/2026) ) 

## When is the Utah annual report due?

Each calendar year by the last day of the entity's anniversary month: the month its formation became effective with the Division or, for a foreign entity, the month its authority to conduct affairs in Utah took effect. It may be filed up to 60 days before that date. The Division may set a different period by rule. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “each calendar year on the last day of the anniversary month” ( Utah Legislature — Utah Code § 16-1a-212, Annual report for division (Effective 10/1/2026) ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Utah?

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

## What happens if the Utah report is late?

The state's page we read does not state a late penalty. Ask the filing office before the date passes.

Virginia Annual Report Due Date and Fee 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · VIRGINIA 

# Virginia annual report due date

 Annual report (Code of Virginia § 13.1-775) : Each year on or before the last day of the month in which the corporation was incorporated or authorized in Virginia (stated as the last day of the twelfth month after that month, then the same date each year). It can be filed no earlier than three months before the due date. The State Corporation Commission can move a due date by 1 to 11 months.
 Annual registration fee (Code of Virginia § 13.1-1062), payment only : Each year on or before the last day of the month in which the LLC was organized or registered in Virginia (stated as the last day of the twelfth month after that month, then the same date each year). Different dates apply to LLCs created by conversion or domestication. The Commission can move a due date by 1 to 11 months. 

From the official Code of Virginia § 13.1-775 page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Annual report (Code of Virginia § 13.1-775)

### Who files it

Domestic corporations and foreign corporations authorized to transact business in Virginia. 
The official page says: “Each domestic corporation, and each foreign corporation authorized to transact business in the Commonwealth” ( Code of Virginia § 13.1-775 — Annual report of domestic and foreign corporations (Virginia LIS) ) 

### When it is due

Each year on or before the last day of the month in which the corporation was incorporated or authorized in Virginia (stated as the last day of the twelfth month after that month, then the same date each year). It can be filed no earlier than three months before the due date. The State Corporation Commission can move a due date by 1 to 11 months. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “on or before the last day of the twelfth month next succeeding the month” ( Code of Virginia § 13.1-775 — Annual report of domestic and foreign corporations (Virginia LIS) ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

The state's page we read does not state a late penalty. Ask the filing office before the date passes. 

## Annual registration fee (Code of Virginia § 13.1-1062), payment only

### Who files it

Domestic LLCs, protected series, and foreign LLCs and foreign protected series registered in Virginia. 
The official page says: “Every domestic limited liability company, every protected series, every foreign limited liability company registered” ( Code of Virginia § 13.1-1062 — Annual registration fees for limited liability companies (Virginia LIS) ) 

### When it is due

Each year on or before the last day of the month in which the LLC was organized or registered in Virginia (stated as the last day of the twelfth month after that month, then the same date each year). Different dates apply to LLCs created by conversion or domestication. The Commission can move a due date by 1 to 11 months. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “on or before the last day of the twelfth month next succeeding the month” ( Code of Virginia § 13.1-775 — Annual report of domestic and foreign corporations (Virginia LIS) ) 

### What it costs

$50 per year. 
The official page says: “by such date in each year thereafter, an annual registration fee of $50” ( Code of Virginia § 13.1-1062 — Annual registration fees for limited liability companies (Virginia LIS) ) 

### If it is late

The state's page we read does not state a late penalty. Ask the filing office before the date passes.

Wisconsin Annual Report Due Date and Late Penalty 

 Skip to content 

STATE FILING · WISCONSIN 

# Wisconsin annual report due date

 Annual Report (domestic entities) : Due each year after the calendar year of registration, during the calendar quarter containing the registration anniversary date; due by the last day of that quarter (March 31, June 30, September 30 or December 31).
 Annual Report (foreign entities) : Due during the first calendar quarter (by March 31) of each year after the calendar year in which the foreign entity registered. 

From the official Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions page, read on 20 November 2026. Your own date depends on when and how your business was formed. 

## Annual Report (domestic entities)

### Who files it

Domestic business corporations (Ch. 180), nonstock corporations (Ch. 181), LLCs (Ch. 183), cooperatives (Ch. 185), LLPs (Ch. 178), LPs (Ch. 179, from 1/1/23), common law trusts (Ch. 226) and agricultural associations (Ch. 100.23). 
The official page says: “Annual reports are required for the following entity types:” ( Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions — Business Entity FAQ ) 

### When it is due

Due each year after the calendar year of registration, during the calendar quarter containing the registration anniversary date; due by the last day of that quarter (March 31, June 30, September 30 or December 31). It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “during the calendar year quarter in which the anniversary date of the registration occurs” ( Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions — Business Entity FAQ ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

An entity that does not file goes delinquent; if not cured for an extended period it risks administrative dissolution. Entities that fail to file for several years are typically administratively dissolved. 
The official page says: “the entity runs the risk of being administratively dissolved” ( Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions — Business Entity FAQ ) 

## Annual Report (foreign entities)

### Who files it

Foreign entities registered to transact business in Wisconsin. 
The official page says: “A foreign entity registered to transact business in this state” ( Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions — Business Entity FAQ ) 

### When it is due

Due during the first calendar quarter (by March 31) of each year after the calendar year in which the foreign entity registered. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “during the first calendar quarter of each year following the calendar year” ( Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions — Business Entity FAQ ) 

### What it costs

The state's page we read does not state the fee. The state shows it when you file. 

### If it is late

Foreign entities that have not filed within four months of the March 31 due date may have their Certificate of Authority/Registration revoked or terminated. 
The official page says: “within four months of the March 31st due date, are subject to having their Certificate” ( Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions — Business Entity FAQ )

Your own due date depends on when and how your business was formed, so the state page is where you confirm it. Once you know it, the renewal reminder calculator works out the reminder dates and gives you a calendar file.

## When is the Wyoming annual report due?

Due on the first day of the anniversary month of the initial filing each year. For example, an entity first filed on May 15 is due May 1 each year. Statutory trust annual reports are due by January 1 each year. It is filed every year. 
The official page says: “due on the first day of the anniversary month of formation.” ( Wyoming Secretary of State — Annual Report Instructions (wyobiz.wyo.gov) ) 

## How much does it cost to file in Wyoming?

The license tax amount is not stated on the state's page. Filing online adds a payment card processing fee of 2.4% (minimum $1) of the filing fee. E-filing is not allowed if the annual report fee is over $500.

# Renewal reminder calculator

Enter the date a license, permit, insurance policy or state filing is due and this lists the days to be reminded: 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before by default, the same schedule as the Obligio app. It also makes a calendar file with those reminders built in. It runs in your browser; nothing you type is sent anywhere. 

 What is due 

 Due date 

 Remind me this many days before 

Whole days, separated by commas. Up to 730. 
 Repeats 
 Does not repeat Every year Every two years 
 Work out reminders Reset 

The calculator needs JavaScript. The rule is simple: subtract each reminder's number of days from the due date. 

## How it works

Reminder date = due date − reminder days, counted in calendar days. The calendar file is a standard .ics event on the due date with one alert per reminder, so Apple Calendar, Google Calendar and Outlook show the alerts without any app. If the date repeats, the file repeats it every year or every two years; check each new date with the issuing authority, because rules and dates change. 

## Questions

 How are the reminder dates worked out? 
Each reminder is the due date minus that many calendar days. A reminder that lands on a weekend is marked, not moved, because rules on weekends and holidays differ by authority. Does this store what I type? 
No. The dates are worked out in your browser and nothing is sent anywhere. The calendar file is made on your device. Which reminder days should I use? 
The defaults, 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before, are the ones the Obligio app uses. Change them to any whole numbers of days up to 730.

Updated: 2026-11-11

ASIC Annual Review Date: Deadlines, Fees and Late Fees | Obligio 

 Skip to content 

GUIDE · AUSTRALIA 

# ASIC annual review date: how to find it, and every deadline that follows it

Your company's ASIC annual review date is the anniversary of the day it was registered, unless ASIC has approved a different date. To see it, search the company on ASIC's free companies and organisations search : the free result shows the registration date and the next review date. On or soon after that date ASIC sends the annual statement. From the review date you have 28 days from the statement's issue date to correct details, and 2 months to pay the fee ($342 for a proprietary company from 1 July 2026) and to pass a solvency resolution. Below are those deadlines worked out for one company, the late fees, and a reminder plan. 

## The four dates that hang off your review date

Each row is ASIC's own rule, from its company annual review page , its late fee page and its deregistration page . The example column is a company registered on 14 March 2019, so its review date is 14 March 2027. 

 Deadlines after the annual review date, with a worked example (review date 14 March 2027, statement issued the same day). 

 What ASIC's rule Example date If you miss it 

 Check the statement and correct any wrong details "Within 28 days" of the statement's issue date 11 April 2027 A late review fee: $102 if up to 1 month late, $428 if more. This is on top of any late lodgement fee for a change you should have lodged within 28 days of it happening. 

 Pay the annual review fee By the due date on the statement, "usually 2 months after the annual review date" 14 May 2027 A late payment fee: $102 if paid up to 1 month late (to 14 June 2027), $428 if later. 

 Directors pass a solvency resolution "Within 2 months of the annual review date", unless the company lodged a financial report with ASIC in the past 12 months 14 May 2027 If none is passed, or it is negative, lodge Form 485 within 7 days (21 May 2027 if none was passed). 

 Fee still unpaid ASIC's "most common reason" to start deregistration: the fee unpaid "for at least 12 months after the due date" From 14 May 2028 ASIC writes to the company and directors, marks it "strike off in progress" and posts a 2-month notice. Paying the outstanding fees may stop it. 

Your own statement's due date overrides this table. If no statement has arrived 15 business days after the review date, ASIC asks you to contact it . 

## What it costs from 1 July 2026

These amounts are from ASIC's fee data for Information Sheet 30, Fees for commonly lodged documents . ASIC says these fees are not subject to GST. 

 Fee Amount 

 Annual review fee, proprietary company $342 

 Annual review fee, special purpose proprietary company (for example a company whose sole purpose is to be trustee of a regulated super fund, such as an SMSF trustee) $70 

 Annual review fee, public company $1,591 

 Late payment or late review fee, up to 1 month late $102 

 Late payment or late review fee, more than 1 month late $428 

 Ten years of review fees paid in advance, proprietary company $2,538 

 Apply to change the review date (Form 488), per company $52 

 Business name renewal, 1 year or 3 years $47 or $108 

### Should you pay ten years in advance?

At today's fee, ten yearly payments would be $3,420 against $2,538 up front. The $2,538 equals about seven and a half years of today's fee. ASIC says "refunds for advance payments are not available". So the rule is: if you are confident the company will exist for at least eight more years and you want one less thing to pay, prepaying saves money. If you might close or sell the company sooner, pay yearly. Prepaying covers the fee only; the details check and the solvency resolution are still due every year. 

## A reminder plan that matches ASIC's deadlines

ASIC sends one statement. The deadlines that cost money are 28 days and 2 months later, so set your reminders against those, not against the review date alone. 

 One week before the review date: check that ASIC will reach you. The statement goes to one address only, in this order: your registered agent, your company officeholder portal account, your nominated mailing address, then the registered office. If any of those is out of date, fix it now. 

 On the review date: download the statement. Read every line against what is true today: addresses, officeholders, share structure and members. 

 Day 21 after the statement is issued: last call for corrections. Lodge them before day 28. 

 Six weeks after the review date: hold the solvency resolution and pay the fee. That leaves about two weeks before both fall due. 

 Afterwards: file the resolution record and the payment receipt with the statement, then set next year's reminders. 

If you keep this on your phone, Obligio has an "ASIC company annual review" template for Australian companies that repeats every year. Each item sends reminders 30, 14, 7 and 1 day before its date, so enter the fee due date and add the 28-day correction date as its own item. It does not read ASIC's register, pay the fee or lodge anything, and the free plan holds three obligations ( Free and Plus ). The plan above works just as well in a paper diary or the spreadsheet tracker . 

## Recording the solvency resolution

ASIC describes the resolution as stating "whether the company can pay its debts when they are due, in the opinion of a majority of the directors", based on good evidence. The company keeps the record; a positive resolution is not sent to ASIC. A sole director might record it like this. This is an example of the content, not legal wording: 

Resolution of the directors of Example Pty Ltd (ACN 000 000 000), passed on 30 April 2027 in respect of the review date 14 March 2027. Having considered the company's bank statements, debts due and expected income for the next 12 months, the directors are of the opinion that there are reasonable grounds to believe the company will be able to pay its debts as and when they become due and payable. Signed: [director], [date]. 

If you cannot honestly say yes, do not pass a positive resolution. Lodge Form 485 within 7 days and get advice from an accountant or insolvency practitioner. 

## Is that invoice really from ASIC?

Private companies send letters and emails about annual reviews and business name renewals that look like invoices. ASIC's scams page says "these providers are not ASIC" and that their notice "may look like an invoice, even though you are not required to pay it". Check four things before paying: 

The sender. ASIC's emails come from an address ending in @asic.gov.au. 

The amount. A fee different from ASIC's published fee (the table above) is a warning sign. 

The method. ASIC does not ask for card details over the phone and does not accept crypto. 

The source. Download the statement from your own ASIC portal login rather than following a link. 

## ABN and business name dates are separate

 Business name. Registered for 1 or 3 years. ASIC emails a renewal notice at least 30 days before it is due, and if you do not renew "ASIC may cancel it" ( renew a business name ). The renewal date is not your company review date. 

 ABN. The Australian Business Register's pages describe updating or cancelling an ABN, not renewing it. Its rule is: "You must update your details within 28 days of becoming aware of changes" ( ABR, Update your ABN details ). It is a separate register, so check it on its own after you move or change directors. 

## When this page does not apply

 You are a sole trader or partnership with no company. There is no ASIC annual review. Your dates are the business name renewal and your ABN details. 

 The company is registered with the ACNC as a charity. ASIC's fee table lists no annual review fee for an entity registered under the ACNC Act. Check the ACNC for its own reporting dates. 

 The company is already "strike off in progress" or deregistered. Act within the 2-month notice: contact ASIC and pay what is outstanding. After deregistration, see ASIC's company reinstatement pages, and speak to an accountant or lawyer. 

 You were late because of something outside your control. ASIC lets you ask it to review a late fee , and it may waive it. 

 You are outside Australia. For US and general renewals see the business licence renewal tracker , and if a date has passed, what happens if a business licence expires . 

## Questions

 How do I find my company's ASIC annual review date? 
Search the company on ASIC's free companies register search. The free result lists the registration date and the next review date. For most companies the review date is the anniversary of the registration date. It is also printed on the annual statement and shown in the company officeholder portal. When is the ASIC annual review fee due? 
By the due date on the annual statement, which ASIC says is usually 2 months after the annual review date. From 1 July 2026 the fee is $342 for a proprietary company. Paying up to 1 month late adds $102; more than 1 month late adds $428. Can I change my company's annual review date? 
Yes, with Form 488 and a $52 fee per company (from 1 July 2026), posted to ASIC. ASIC considers it where companies share an ultimate holding company, an officeholder or a responsible entity, or in exceptional circumstances. A date that has already passed cannot be changed. A new date earlier than the current one applies immediately; a later one applies after the current review. Do I have to send ASIC a solvency resolution? 
No, if it is positive. The directors pass it within 2 months of the review date and the company keeps the record. You only lodge Form 485, within 7 days, if the resolution is negative or if none was passed within the 2 months. Companies that lodged a financial report with ASIC in the past 12 months are exempt. Does an ABN have a review or renewal date? 
The ABR's pages describe updating or cancelling an ABN, not renewing it. The obligation it states is to update your details within 28 days of becoming aware of a change. A registered business name is different: it is renewed for 1 or 3 years, and ASIC emails the renewal notice at least 30 days before it is due. 

## Sources

 ASIC, Change a company's annual review date

 ASIC, Scams impersonating ASIC

All sources were read on 11 November 2026. ASIC's fee table is set from 1 July each year; confirm the amount on your own statement. This page is organisational guidance, not legal, tax or insolvency advice. 

If you want these dates on your phone, Obligio is free for your first three obligations: download on the App Store or get it on Google Play . Questions about the app go to support .

Business License Renewal Tracker: Template & Rules | Obligio 

 Skip to content 

GUIDE 

# Business license renewal tracker: what to record, when to set reminders

A business license renewal tracker is one list of every dated license, permit, registration and policy your business holds, with the expiry date, the issuing agency, the renewal window and the person responsible on each row. The first reminder goes on the day the agency lets you renew, the second 30 days before expiry and the last a week before. Below is the template as a table you can copy, a list of what commonly expires and how often (with the agencies' own pages linked), and a rule for deciding whether a calendar is enough or you need a dedicated tracker. The examples are from the United States. Australians spell it licence; the web address keeps that spelling so both can find this page. 

## What to record for each license

The U.S. Small Business Administration puts the problem in one sentence: "Some licenses and permits expire after a set period of time. Keep close track of when you need to renew them — it's often easier to renew than it is to apply for a new one" ( SBA, Apply for licenses and permits ). Tracking the date alone is not enough, because on renewal day you also need the login, the fee, the number and the proof. Record these for each row: 

 Obligation : what it is, in your own words, and the entity it belongs to if you have more than one. 

 Issuing agency and the page or portal you renew on. 

 License or account number , so you can find it in the portal. 

 Expires on : the date printed on the document. Washington's Department of Revenue, for example, prints it in the upper right of the business license ( WA DOR, Business Licensing and renewals FAQs ). 

 Cycle : annual, two years, four years, five years, or one-off. 

 Renewal window opens : the earliest date the agency accepts a renewal. 

 Reminder dates : the three dates you actually set. 

 Fee last paid , so you can budget the next one. 

 Owner : the one person who does it. 

 Proof stored : where the current certificate or policy lives. 

 Status : current, renewal in progress, or overdue. 

## The tracker template (copy it)

Select the table, copy it into a spreadsheet or document, and replace the example rows with your own. The dates below are placeholders chosen to show how the columns relate; they are not anyone's real deadlines. 

 Business license renewal tracker. Example rows only: replace every value with your own. 

 Obligation Issuing agency / portal Number Expires on Cycle Renewal window opens Reminder dates Fee last paid Owner Proof stored Status 

 State business license (example) State revenue department, online portal UBI 000-000-000 2027-03-31 Annual 2027-02-01 (two months early) 2027-02-01, 2027-03-01, 2027-03-24 $ (your receipt) Owner's name Compliance/Licenses/state-2026.pdf Current 

 Reseller / sales tax permit (example) State revenue department A000000000 2029-12-31 4 years 2029-10-01 2029-10-01, 2029-12-01, 2029-12-24 $0 Bookkeeper's name Compliance/Tax/reseller-permit.pdf Current 

 Fictitious business name / DBA (example) County clerk FBN 2026-000000 2031-06-14 5 years Check county page 2031-03-15, 2031-05-15, 2031-06-07 $ (your receipt) Owner's name Compliance/Entity/fbn-filed-2026.pdf Current 

 Cosmetology establishment license (example) State licensing board, online EST 000000 2028-08-31 2 years 2028-06-09 (83 days early) 2028-06-09, 2028-08-01, 2028-08-24 $ (your receipt) Manager's name Compliance/Licenses/establishment.pdf Current 

 General liability policy (example) Insurer / broker Policy no. 2027-05-01 Annual Ask broker 2027-02-01, 2027-04-01, 2027-04-24 $ (premium) Owner's name Compliance/Insurance/GL-2026.pdf Renewal in progress 

Print it with the browser's print command: the header and footer are hidden on paper. Keep the completed version with your other business records. 

## What commonly expires, and how often

Cycles are set by each agency and differ from state to state, so treat the table below as examples to check against, not a schedule. Each row links to the agency's own page, read on the day this was written. 

 Type of obligation Verified example 

 State or local business license Washington: a business with a state or city endorsement through the Business Licensing Service renews its license annually. The department sends a courtesy reminder one month before expiry, but the renewal is due by the printed date whether or not the notice arrives, and late renewals incur a late penalty fee ( WA DOR ). 

 Sales tax permit or reseller permit Washington reseller permits "are generally valid for four years", or two years in listed cases such as contractors and businesses open under 12 months ( WA DOR, Reseller permits ). Colorado sales tax licenses run two years; the current period began January 1, 2026, after all prior licenses expired December 31, 2025, with a $16 renewal fee per physical location ( Colorado DOR ). 

 Annual report or statement of information Oregon: "Your renewal is due on the anniversary date of the original filing", with a notice sent about 45 days ahead ( Oregon SOS ). California: a statutory six-month filing window tied to the month of formation; failure may bring Franchise Tax Board penalties and suspension or forfeiture ( California SOS ). 

 Franchise tax Delaware domestic corporations file the annual report and pay franchise tax on or before March 1; missing it costs $200 plus 1.5 percent interest per month ( Delaware Division of Corporations ). Texas franchise tax reports are due May 15, with a $50 penalty on each late report ( Texas Comptroller ). 

 DBA or fictitious business name Los Angeles County: a fictitious business name statement "expires five years from the date it is filed with the County Clerk" and the renewal must be filed before expiry ( LA County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk ). 

 Professional and trade licenses California Board of Barbering and Cosmetology licenses have a two-year period, can be renewed up to 83 days before expiry, and carry a $25 delinquent fee for individual licenses ( Board of Barbering and Cosmetology ). 

 Federal certifications EPA lead-safe (RRP) firm certifications "are good for five years"; the firm must apply for re-certification at least 90 days before expiry, and a lapsed firm may not conduct renovations until EPA approves a new application ( EPA ). 

 Insurance and inspections The renewal date is on the policy's declarations page or the inspection certificate. If the certificate does not state the next due date, ask the agency or inspector and write it down. 

 Does not expire: EIN The IRS does not describe an EIN as expiring. It says it "can't cancel it, but we can deactivate it", and that a new EIN is generally needed only when ownership or structure changes ( IRS ). Leave it off the tracker. 

## How far ahead to set reminders

Agencies' own notices arrive late in the cycle: one month before expiry in Washington, about 45 days in Oregon, and about 90 days for a Washington reseller permit that will not auto-renew. Several also state when they will take a renewal: Washington two months early, California's cosmetology board 83 days, and EPA requires the lead-safe application 90 or more days before expiry. So use three reminders: 

 First : the day the renewal window opens. If the agency does not publish one, use 90 days before expiry. 

 Second : 30 days before expiry. This is roughly when most agency notices arrive, so if yours has not, something is wrong with your address on file. 

 Last : 7 days before expiry. By this one the renewal should already be done and the new certificate filed. 

When the first reminder fires, how to renew a business license lists what to gather, how to submit and how to confirm the renewal went through. 

If you use Obligio, note how it fits this rule. The app sends reminders 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before the date you enter, with notifications enabled. For a license whose window opens two or three months out, enter the day you intend to renew as the deadline, not the printed expiry, so the 30-day reminder lands when the window opens. 

## Calendar or dedicated tracker? A decision rule

Count the rows in your tracker, then apply this: 

 A calendar is enough if you have three or fewer dated obligations, all on a yearly or shorter cycle, one person is responsible, and nothing needs a stored document at renewal time. Put the three reminder dates on each one and you are done. 

 Use a dedicated tracker (the spreadsheet above, or an app) if any of these is true: more than three obligations; any cycle longer than a year, because a reminder set four or five years out only survives if that calendar and that phone do; renewals that need a certificate or policy attached; more than one person doing renewals; or more than one agency portal and login to keep straight. 

The multi-year items are the ones that catch people out. A four-year reseller permit or a five-year fictitious name statement is renewed so rarely that nobody remembers how, which is why the "renewal window opens" and "proof stored" columns exist. 

If you keep the tracker in a spreadsheet, the compliance tracking spreadsheet guide has formulas that count the days left and a script that emails you when a date is close. 

## Where Obligio fits

 Obligio is a business compliance tracker for iPhone and Android that holds the same rows as the template: each obligation with its due date, category, and the reminders described above. It shows current, upcoming and overdue items in a dashboard and calendar ( features ). The Free plan tracks up to three obligations, which matches the calendar case in the rule above. Plus adds unlimited obligations, attached document evidence so the certificate sits with its deadline, and recurring obligations that roll forward when you mark one complete ( Free and Plus ; prices are shown in the app). It also offers a catalogue of selected US federal obligations with links to official sources and the date each was last reviewed. Coverage is limited: you add your own state, local and industry requirements, and it does not tell you every requirement for your business, give legal or tax advice, or file anything on your behalf. The template above works without it. 

## When this page does not apply

If you need to know which licenses your business must hold, start with your Secretary of State's site; the SBA says to "research your own state, county, and city regulations" because "industry requirements often vary by state" ( SBA ). 

If a renewal has already lapsed, go straight to the agency's page or phone line; penalties and reinstatement rules are theirs, and some, like the EPA example above, stop you working until approved. What happens if a business license expires sets out the three consequences with the agencies' wording and a fix-it plan. 

For tax filing deadlines rather than license renewals, see the small business compliance calendar on this site, which lists the federal dates with the IRS's own wording, or ask a CPA. 

If you are in Australia, the Australian Government's Australian Business Licence and Information Service lists licences by location and activity. The template still works; the examples do not. 

For anything that turns on your entity type or a notice an agency sent you, ask a licensed attorney or accountant. This page is organizational guidance, not legal or tax advice. 

## Questions

 Does an EIN need renewing? 
No renewal is described by the IRS. Its EIN page says the IRS cannot cancel an EIN, only deactivate it, and that a new one is generally needed only when the entity's ownership or structure changes. 
 How early can I renew a business license? 
It depends on the agency. Washington's Department of Revenue accepts business license renewals up to two months before the printed expiry date. California's Board of Barbering and Cosmetology accepts renewals up to 83 days early. The EPA requires lead-safe firm re-certification at least 90 days before expiry. Record each agency's window in the tracker. 
 What happens if I miss a renewal? 
Each agency sets its own consequence. From the pages linked above: Delaware charges a corporation $200 plus 1.5 percent monthly interest for a missed March 1 filing; Texas assesses $50 per late franchise tax report; California's Secretary of State warns of Franchise Tax Board penalties and suspension or forfeiture; a lapsed EPA lead-safe firm cannot conduct renovations until re-approved. Check your agency's page and renew as soon as you can. 
 Why is the web address spelled licence? 
American English spells the noun license. Australian and British English spell it licence, as the Australian Government's Australian Business Licence and Information Service does. The address keeps that spelling so readers in both places can find the page; the text uses the US spelling because the examples are American.

Updated: 2026-11-25

Home-Based Business License Requirements: Checklist | Obligio 

 Skip to content 

GUIDE 

# Home-based business license requirements: a checklist in the order to do it, and what renews

A business run from home usually needs the same city or county business license as a shop, plus permission to use a house for business. That permission is the zoning part: a home occupation permit, or a zoning check built into the license application. On top of that, add only what your work triggers. Selling goods needs a state seller's permit. Trading under a made-up name needs a DBA (fictitious business name) filing. A regulated trade needs its state license. Employees or an LLC need an EIN. Check your homeowners or renter's insurance too, because it rarely covers business liability. Do zoning first: it is the step that can say no. 

## The checklist, in the order to do it

 What a home-based business may need, who issues it, and whether it renews 

 Step Issued by You need it if Renews? 

 1. Lease, HOA or deed rules Your landlord or homeowners association You rent, or live where an HOA or deed restricts business use or signs No, but rules can change at each lease 

 2. Zoning: home occupation permit or sign-off City or county planning or zoning office Almost always; the rules limit visitors, staff, deliveries and signs Sometimes re-checked at every license renewal 

 3. General business license or tax registration City or county Almost always, even for online-only work Yes, often yearly or every two years 

 4. DBA / fictitious business name County clerk or state You trade under a name that is not your own legal name Yes in many places (five years in California) 

 5. State seller's permit State tax agency You sell physical goods that are taxable where you sell Usually no, but returns are due on a schedule 

 6. State professional or trade license State licensing board Your work is regulated (cosmetology, childcare, contracting, food) Yes, on the board's cycle 

 7. EIN IRS (free) You hire employees, form an LLC, partnership or corporation, or owe certain federal taxes No 

 8. Insurance Your insurer You keep stock or equipment at home, or anyone visits for business Yes, yearly 

Sources for each row are named in the sections below and listed at the end. The SBA notes that zoning ordinances "can still apply even to home-based businesses" ( SBA, Launch your business ). 

## What home occupation rules actually say: three cities

Every city writes its own limits. These three show the range. Read your own city's page before you sign a lease or print a sign. 

 Home business rules as published by each city, read 25 November 2026 

 Rule Chicago, IL Los Angeles, CA Columbia, SC 

 License City business license required; listed fee $1,000 Business Tax Registration Certificate from the Office of Finance City business license 

 Non-resident employees working in the home No more than one One Set by zoning on the home occupation form 

 Customers No more than 2 at a time, 10 in 24 hours One client visit per hour, 8 am to 8 pm Set by zoning 

 Deliveries One bulk delivery a day, 8 am to 6 pm; no tractor trailers Two deliveries or pick-ups a day Set by zoning 

 Signs No exterior signage Nothing visible from outside Set by zoning 

 Not allowed at home Food uses, barber shops, massage, medical uses, animal care, vehicle repair and others Mechanized equipment not normal in a home; commercial vehicles parked on site Checked by zoning 

 Renewal Every two years Yearly renewal due January 1, delinquent the first business day of March All licenses expire April 30; home occupation form resubmitted with each renewal 

From City of Chicago, Home Based Business , LA Business Navigator, Home-Based Businesses and City of Columbia, Business License Renewal . The Los Angeles renewal dates are from the Office of Finance, Business Tax Information FAQ . Confirm fees with each city, as they change. 

## The renewal trap: zoning is checked again

Most checklists stop once the license arrives. For a home business, the renewal is where things slip. Columbia, South Carolina, says all business licenses expire on April 30, renewal forms are mailed early in the year, and a home occupation must resubmit its home occupation form with the renewal "for re-validation by zoning". Paying late costs 5%, plus another 5% on the first of each month until paid. Not receiving the form is not a defense. A name or address change must be reported within ten days. 

Los Angeles has a quieter version of the same trap. A business with $100,000 or less in gross receipts may qualify for the city's Small Business Exemption, but the Office of Finance must receive the renewal form on time to grant it. The renewal is due January 1 and delinquent on the first business day of March ( LA Office of Finance FAQ ). Miss the form and a business that owed nothing can owe penalties. 

So the dates to put in a calendar the day each item arrives are: the business license expiry, any DBA expiry, the state license expiry, and the insurance renewal. Each one gets a reminder 30 days ahead, and the business license gets a note to fetch the zoning form too. 

## Worked example: candles sold from a Los Angeles apartment

Maya makes candles at home in Los Angeles. She sells them online, at weekend craft fairs, and to a few customers who collect from her door. She trades as "Maya Lane Candles". 

 Lease. She checks her lease for a business-use clause before anything else. 

 Zoning. Collections fit the city's limit of one client visit per hour between 8 am and 8 pm. She keeps no sign in the window. 

 City. She registers for a Business Tax Registration Certificate, which the city says every business in Los Angeles needs. Her sales are well under $100,000, so she files the yearly renewal by January 1 to keep the Small Business Exemption. 

 Seller's permit. California requires a seller's permit once you make three or more sales of merchandise in 12 months, from home or a store ( CDTFA, Tax Guide for Home-Based Businesses ). Her craft-fair sales are her own, so she needs one even though a marketplace collects tax on its own sales. 

 DBA. "Maya Lane Candles" is not her legal name, so she files a fictitious business name statement with the Los Angeles County Clerk. Filed on 1 December 2026, it expires on 1 December 2031. Renewal costs $26 and needs no newspaper publication ( LA County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk, Renewals ). 

 EIN. As a sole owner with no employees, she does not need one. The IRS requires an EIN if you have employees or operate an LLC, partnership or corporation ( IRS, Employer identification number ). She can still get one free for banking. 

 Insurance. Her renter's policy is unlikely to cover a customer hurt at her door. She asks about a home business endorsement. 

Her calendar then holds four renewal dates: the city business tax every January 1, the DBA on 1 December 2031, the renter's policy, and her sales tax return dates. 

## Insurance: the gap most home businesses miss

The Insurance Information Institute says a homeowners policy may cover business equipment only up to about $2,500 at home and $250 away from it, and usually does not cover business liability at all, such as a client who falls on your stairs ( Triple-I, Insuring your home business ). It describes three fixes: an endorsement on the home policy, separate business policies, or a small businessowners package. Ask your agent which fits. 

### Home business checklist: print and tick

Lease, HOA or deed checked for business-use and sign rules 

City zoning rules read: staff ___ visitors ___ deliveries ___ signs ___ 

Home occupation permit or zoning sign-off: number ______ date ___ / ___ / ______ 

City or county business license: expires ___ / ___ / ______ 

DBA filed (if trading under another name): expires ___ / ___ / ______ 

State seller's permit (if selling goods): number ______ returns due ______ 

State professional or trade license (if regulated): expires ___ / ___ / ______ 

EIN (if employees or an LLC): ______ 

Insurance asked about home business cover: renews ___ / ___ / ______ 

Each expiry date in a calendar with a 30-day reminder 

Note on the license reminder: resubmit zoning form if the city asks 

## When this page does not apply

 You make food at home to sell. Most home occupation rules exclude it. Look up your state's cottage food rules; Chicago, for example, points to a Cottage Food Registration with its Department of Public Health. 

 You are a contractor working from home. Your state board's license matters most. See contractor license renewal dates and reminders . 

 You already have the license and need to renew it. See how to renew a business license . 

 A date has already passed. Read what happens if a business license expires . 

 You need the state's annual report date for an LLC. Find it in annual report due dates by state . 

## Keeping the dates after the setup

Once the list is done, what remains is four or five dates on different cycles. Our small business compliance calendar adds the federal tax dates, and the business license renewal tracker guide lists what to record for each item. Obligio, our app for iPhone and Android, is one way to hold them: it reminds you 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before each date and shows anything past due as overdue. It does not know your city's rules or check any agency for you. 

## Questions

 Do I need a business license if I only work online from home? 
Usually yes. Cities and counties license the business, not the shopfront. Chicago, for example, says a City of Chicago business license is required to operate a business out of your home. What working online changes is the zoning side: with no visitors, deliveries or signs, a home office normally fits the home occupation rules easily. 
 Does my homeowners insurance cover my home business? 
Often only a little. The Insurance Information Institute says a homeowners policy may cover business equipment only up to about $2,500 in the home and $250 away from it, and usually does not cover business liability at all. Ask your insurer about a home business endorsement or a separate policy. 
 Do I have to renew a home occupation permit? 
It depends on the city. Chicago issues home occupation licenses for two years. In Columbia, South Carolina, every business license expires on April 30 and a home business must resubmit its home occupation form with each renewal so zoning can check it again. Put the renewal date in your calendar the day the license arrives.

# Compliance software for small business: which kind you need, what it costs, and when a spreadsheet is enough

"Compliance software" is sold for four different jobs, and most small businesses need only one or two of them. If your worry is license, permit and insurance deadlines, you need a deadline tracker; a free spreadsheet works for about ten items. State annual reports are handled by a registered agent service; Northwest charges $125 a year. Payroll tax filings are handled by your payroll provider; Gusto files Forms 941, 940 and W-2. Only if a customer asks you for SOC 2 or HIPAA evidence do you need a security platform such as Vanta or Drata, and neither publishes prices. The table below sorts the jobs, with prices checked on 16 November 2026. 

## First, name the job: four kinds of compliance software

"Best compliance software" lists mix these together, so a two-person trade business ends up reading about audit frameworks it will never need. Find your row first. 

 Prices are from each vendor's own page, read 16 November 2026. "Quote only" means the vendor publishes no price. 

 If the thing you must not miss is… The kind of tool Examples and published price A spreadsheet is enough when… 

 License, permit, certificate and insurance expiry dates Deadline or expiration tracker Expiration Reminder: from $49 a month, or $528 a year billed annually, for 150 items. Harbor Compliance License Manager: quote only (demo). One person renews everything and there are fewer than about ten dated items 

 State annual or biennial reports, registered agent mail Registered agent service Northwest Registered Agent: $125 a year per state ($100 per state for five or more), with annual report reminders You are your own registered agent, operate in one state, and put the report date in your calendar 

 Payroll tax deposits and forms (941, 940, W-2, 1099) Payroll provider Gusto Simple: $49 a month plus $6 per person. Gusto Business Compliance add-on: $85 a month per state on an annual contract Rarely. Payroll tax filing is the job most worth handing over 

 Security or privacy audits a customer asks for (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA) Compliance automation (GRC) platform Vanta: quote only. Drata: quote only No customer, contract or regulator has asked you for one 

## Deadline trackers, for licenses, permits and insurance

This is knowing that the city license expires on 30 April and the liability policy on 1 July, and being told early enough to act. Here the cheapest option works longest. 

 A spreadsheet. Free, but a dated cell reminds no one. Our compliance tracking spreadsheet guide has the formulas, color rules and a short Google Sheets script that emails you when a date is near. 

 Expiration Reminder. A dedicated expiry tracker. Starter is $49 a month for 150 items, Professional $99 for 600. Every plan includes unlimited admin users and file storage, SMS reminders, iOS and Android apps, and a 14-day trial with no card. It suits a business tracking many people's certificates, vehicles or sites, where more than one person needs the list. 

 Harbor Compliance License Manager. It tracks the "status and renewals of firm and individual licenses", stores documents against each license and adds a database of licensing requirements by state. Harbor says it is built for "compliance professionals and administrative teams". No price is published; you book a demo. It suits a firm licensed in many states, not a single-location shop. 

For what to record against each license and when to set reminders, see the business license renewal tracker . 

## Registered agents, for state annual reports

An LLC or corporation must keep a registered agent and, in most states, file an annual or biennial report. Northwest warns that a missed report can cost good standing. A registered agent service receives the state's mail. Northwest charges $125 a year, or $100 a year per state for five or more states. It says it will remind you as the deadline approaches and "take care of the requirement for you". Ask what each filing costs before relying on that. You can be your own agent if you have an address in the state and are there in business hours; then the report date is one more row in your tracker. Federal and annual dates by entity type are in the small business compliance calendar . 

## Payroll providers, for payroll tax filings

With employees, your most frequent deadlines are payroll tax deposits and quarterly returns. A payroll provider files these; no tracker does. Gusto's pricing page says it files "federal, state, and local payroll tax forms on your company's behalf (things like Form W-2, Form 1099, Form 940, Form 941, Form 8974, and others)". Simple costs $49 a month plus $6 per person; Plus and Premium cost more. Its Business Compliance add-on, which tracks "state tax registrations, annual reports, and agency mail", is $85 a month per state on an annual contract. 

## Compliance automation platforms, for security audits

Vanta and Drata automate evidence for security and privacy frameworks. Vanta lists SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA and others. Drata's Foundation plan is "Limited to SOC 2, ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials, HIPAA, and GDPR". Vanta offers "personalized pricing" after a demo; Drata's plans also lead to a demo, with no price shown. You need one when a customer's contract or security questionnaire asks for a SOC 2 report, or a regulator expects one. If nobody has asked, this row is not yours. 

## A decision rule you can apply today

List and count every dated obligation: licenses, permits, policies, certificates, reports, filings. 

Payroll? Use a payroll provider for the tax filings, whatever else you decide. 

An LLC or corporation in more than one state, or no reliable in-state address? Use a registered agent service. One state with an address? Track the report date yourself. 

For the licenses and policies left: under about ten items and one person responsible, a spreadsheet with reminders or a phone tracker. More items or more people, a team tracker such as Expiration Reminder. Many states, ask Harbor for a demo. 

A customer asked for SOC 2, ISO 27001 or HIPAA evidence? Then, and only then, get quotes from Vanta and Drata. 

## Worked example: a two-employee cleaning company in one state

One-state LLC, two people on payroll, a city license, general liability and workers' compensation policies. The owner is the registered agent. 

 Prices as published 16 November 2026. Government filing and license fees are extra in every row. 

 Job Choice Cost a year 

 Payroll taxes and W-2s Gusto Simple, 2 people: $49 + 2 × $6 = $61 a month $732 

 State annual report Owner is the agent; date goes in the tracker $0 

 City license, two policies, annual report date (4 items) Spreadsheet with the reminder script $0 

 Security audit platform Not needed; no customer has asked $0 

 Total software spend $732 

Expiration Reminder's Starter plan would add $528 a year for 4 of its 150 items; it is built for a bigger list than this. Hiring Northwest as agent would add $125. Worth it if the owner works from home and wants that address off the public record. 

## Five questions to ask before you pay for any of them

Does it file anything, or only remind you? Most trackers only remind. 

Is it priced per item, person, state, or by quote? Price it at next year's size. 

Who gets the reminder, how, and can a second person get it? 

Can you attach the certificate to the deadline, so the proof sits with the date? 

Can you export your list if you cancel? A tracker you cannot leave is a new risk.

Obligio is a deadline tracker for iPhone and Android, in the first row of the table. It reminds you 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before each date you enter, with notifications enabled. With Plus you can attach documents and have recurring obligations roll forward. It is built for one owner on a phone: no web dashboard, no shared team access, and it files nothing. Its suggested catalogue covers only selected US federal obligations. The free plan tracks three obligations, so the four-item example above would need Plus or a spreadsheet. Everything on this page works without it. 

## When this page does not apply

 You do not yet know which licenses you need. Start with the SBA's licenses and permits guide and your state's business portal, then come back to choose a tracker. 

 A license has already lapsed. See what happens if a business license expires and fix that before buying anything. 

 You are in a regulated field such as healthcare, financial services or cannabis. The rules there are specific; ask a licensed attorney or a compliance adviser in that field. 

 Your company is Australian. See the ASIC annual review date guide . 

## Questions

 What is the cheapest compliance software for a small business? 
A spreadsheet with a reminder script costs nothing and works for about ten dated obligations tracked by one person. Of the paid tools checked on 16 November 2026, Northwest's registered agent service is $125 a year and Expiration Reminder starts at $528 a year billed annually. Harbor Compliance, Vanta and Drata publish no prices. 
 Do I need SOC 2 compliance software? 
Only if a customer, contract or regulator asks you for a SOC 2 report or similar evidence. Platforms such as Vanta and Drata exist for that job and quote prices after a demo. A business that only needs to keep licenses and insurance current does not need one.

Compliance Tracking Spreadsheet vs Tracker App | Obligio

# Compliance tracking spreadsheet or tracker app: make the spreadsheet work, and know when to switch

A spreadsheet is a good compliance tracker for a small business if it does three things without you remembering to look: counts the days left on every license, permit and policy, turns a row red or amber when a date is close, and sends you a reminder. Neither Google Sheets nor Excel does the third by default; a dated cell never notifies anyone. Below are the formulas and color rules to copy (they work in both), a free template file, a short script that makes Google Sheets email you, and a rule for when the spreadsheet has done its job and something else should take over. 

## What a spreadsheet does well, and the one thing it does not do

A spreadsheet is free, you already know it, everyone can open it, and you control every column. For five or ten dated obligations it is often all you need. What it cannot do by itself is tell you a date is coming. Google's help page lists what Sheets can notify you about: comments, changes made by other people ("Any changes are made"), and form submissions. You "won't get notifications when you make changes" yourself, and nothing on the page covers a date in a cell ( Google Docs Editors Help, Manage your notifications ). So a spreadsheet tracker works only as long as someone opens it. The formulas below make that look quick; the script removes the need. 

## The columns and formulas (copy them)

For what each column means and why it is there, see the business license renewal tracker guide. This sheet adds three calculated columns on the right. Put your headings in row 1 and your first obligation in row 2, then fill the formulas down. 

 Columns A to J. A to G are typed in; H, I and J are formulas (shown for row 2). 

 Column Heading What goes in it 

 A Obligation Business license, reseller permit, liability policy, annual report 

 B Agency / portal Who issues it and where you renew 

 C Expires on The date printed on the document, entered as a date 

 D Cycle (months) 12, 24, 48, 60 

 E Window opens (days before expiry) How early the agency lets you renew. Blank if it does not say 

 F Owner The one person who renews it 

 G Proof stored Where the current certificate lives 

 H Days left =IF(C2="","",DAYS(C2,TODAY())) 

 I Status =IF(C2="","",IF(H2<0,"Overdue",IF(H2<=30,"Due within 30 days",IF(H2<=IF(E2="",90,E2),"Window open","Current")))) 

 J Next reminder =IF(C2="","",IF(TODAY()<=C2-IF(E2="",90,MAX(E2,30)),C2-IF(E2="",90,MAX(E2,30)),IF(TODAY()<=C2-30,C2-30,IF(TODAY()<=C2-7,C2-7,"Now")))) 

How they work: 

 Days left uses DAYS(end, start), which returns a plain number in both programs, so a negative number means overdue. 

 Status gives one of four words. "Window open" uses your column E; if E is blank it uses 90 days, the default first reminder in the renewal tracker guide. 

 Next reminder gives the next of three dates: the day the window opens (never later than 30 days out), 30 days before expiry, and 7 days before. Format column J as a date. "Now" means all three have passed and the renewal should already be under way. 

Prefer not to type them? Download the template (CSV) with these headings, the formulas filled in, and three example rows to replace. Open it in Excel, or in Google Sheets with File, Import. If a formula shows as text, paste it from the table above. 

## Color rules: red for overdue, amber for 30 days

Select A2:J200, then add two rules that use a formula. In Google Sheets: Format, Conditional formatting, "Custom formula is" ( Google, Use conditional formatting rules ). In Excel: Home, Conditional Formatting, New Rule, "Use a formula to determine which cells to format"; the formula "must return True or False" ( Microsoft, Use conditional formatting ). 

Red fill: =AND($H2<>"",$H2<0) 

Amber fill: =AND($H2<>"",$H2>=0,$H2<=30) 

The dollar sign before H keeps every cell in the row looking at its own Days left, so the whole row changes color. The $H2<>"" part stops blank rows turning red. Then sort by column H, smallest first, so the most urgent row is always at the top. 

## Make Google Sheets email you

Google Apps Script can run a function on a timer: "Time-driven triggers allow scripts to execute at specific times or intervals" ( Google, Installable triggers ). This one checks the sheet once a day and emails you any row due within 30 days or already overdue. It works out the days itself, so it does not rely on the sheet having recalculated. 

Name the tab Tracker (bottom of the sheet). Keep the columns in the order above. 

Extensions, Apps Script. Delete what is there, paste the code below, and put your email address in SEND_TO. 

Save, then click Run once. Google asks you to authorize the script to read the sheet and send email as you; that prompt is expected. 

Open Triggers (the clock icon), Add Trigger, choose emailDueSoon , event source Time-driven, and a daily timer. 

 // Emails you every row that expires within 30 days or has expired.
var SHEET_NAME = 'Tracker';
var SEND_TO = 'you@example.com'; // your address

function emailDueSoon() {
 var rows = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet()
 .getSheetByName(SHEET_NAME).getDataRange().getValues();
 var today = new Date();
 today.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
 var lines = [];
 for (var i = 1; i < rows.length; i++) {
 var name = rows[i][0], expires = rows[i][2], owner = rows[i][5];
 if (!name || !(expires instanceof Date)) continue;
 var daysLeft = Math.round((expires - today) / 86400000);
 if (daysLeft <= 30) {
 lines.push(name + ': ' + (daysLeft < 0 ? 'OVERDUE by ' + (-daysLeft) + ' days'
 : daysLeft + ' days left') + ' (owner: ' + owner + ')');
 }
 }
 if (lines.length) {
 MailApp.sendEmail(SEND_TO, lines.length + ' compliance item(s) due within 30 days',
 lines.join('\n'));
 }
} 

Three limits to know. A free Google account can send email to 100 recipients a day from scripts, far more than this needs ( Google, Apps Script quotas ). Triggers always run "under the creator's account", so if that person leaves, the emails stop ( Google, Installable triggers ). And set the sheet's time zone (File, Settings) and the script's (Project Settings) to the same place, or a date can be a day out. Excel has no equivalent built in; there, put the dates from column J in your calendar. 

## Spreadsheet, phone app or audit platform: which fits

 Spreadsheet (this page) Compliance tracker app Audit / framework platform 

 Built for A list of dated obligations you control Licenses, permits, policies and filings for one business Controls, risks and evidence for frameworks such as SOC 2 and ISO 27001 

 Reminders Only with the script, or by copying dates to a calendar The main reason to use one; check that it reaches your phone Through the platform's automations, once you set them up 

 Documents A file path or link in a cell Depends on the app; check before you choose Evidence linked to each control 

 Recurring dates You type the new date after each renewal Depends on the app; check before you choose Depends on how the base is built 

 Cost Free Check the store listing; some have a free tier Check the vendor 

 Fits One person, up to about ten items, a desk routine Owner-operators who live on their phone, or several staff renewals Companies preparing for a formal audit 

Example of the third column, checked November 7, 2026: Airtable's compliance tracking template describes SOC 2 and ISO 27001 tabs, a risk register and a corrective action log ( Airtable ). It suits a team running audits; a café renewing a food permit and a liability policy needs far less. 

## When to stop using the spreadsheet: a rule

Keep the spreadsheet while all of these are true: 

One person owns it and opens it at least weekly, or the script is running. 

There are fewer than about ten rows, so a glance shows everything. 

Nobody needs the certificate from their phone at the counter or on a job site. 

Switch when any one stops being true, and especially when renewals are shared between people, when the script's owner may leave, or when you have missed a date the sheet knew about. The sheet was right; nobody was looking. That is the failure a reminder tool exists for. 

One option is Obligio , our app for iPhone and Android. It holds the same rows and sends reminders 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before each date, with notifications on. The Free plan tracks three obligations; Plus adds unlimited obligations, attached documents and recurring obligations that roll forward when completed ( Free and Plus ). It does not import a spreadsheet, so moving means typing each row once. It does not tell you which licenses your business needs or file anything for you. If your sheet is working, keep it. 

## When this page does not apply

If you do not yet know which licenses and filings your business needs, start with the SBA's licenses and permits guide and your state's Secretary of State. A tracker only holds what you put in it. 

For federal tax filing dates by entity type, use the small business compliance calendar . 

If a date in your sheet has already passed, read what happens if a business license expires and contact the agency today. 

For questions about what a rule requires of your business, ask a licensed attorney or accountant. This page is organizational guidance, not legal or tax advice. 

## Questions

 Can Google Sheets send me a reminder when a date is near? 
Not on its own. Google's notification settings for Sheets cover comments, edits by other people and form submissions, not dates in cells. To get an email when a date is near you need a short Apps Script with a time-driven trigger, like the one above. 
 Does the template work in Excel? 
Yes. The formulas use IF, DAYS, MAX and TODAY, which exist in both Excel and Google Sheets. The email script is Google Sheets only; in Excel, put the reminder dates in your calendar instead. 
 Should I calculate the next expiry date with a formula? 
Only as a placeholder. =EDATE(C2,D2) gives a date D2 months after C2 ( Microsoft, EDATE ; Google, EDATE ), but the date that counts is the one printed on the renewed license or policy. Replace the placeholder with that date when the new document arrives.

If you would rather have the reminders on your phone than in a script, Obligio is free for your first three obligations: download on the App Store or get it on Google Play . Questions about the app go to support .
