Contractor License Renewal: Dates, Late Fees, Reminders | Obligio 

 Skip to content 

GUIDE FOR TRADES 

# Contractor license renewal: when the board writes, what late costs, and a reminder plan that covers the bond and insurance too

A contractor license renews on a fixed cycle, usually every two years, and the board's own notice arrives late: about 60 days before expiry in California, as little as 30 days in Texas. Renewing late costs half as much again in both states, and work done while the license is expired counts as unlicensed. So set your own reminders at 90, 60, 45, 30 and 7 days before the date, and set separate ones for the bond and insurance, because a cancelled bond can suspend the license in the middle of the cycle. The table below has the rules for four states, read on the boards' own pages on 18 November 2026. 

## Four states: cycle, notice, late cost, and what else is checked

Licensing is by state, and often by trade within a state. These four are examples to show how much the rules differ. Your own board's renewal page is the authority. 

 Read on each board's or legislature's own page, 18 November 2026. Fees change; confirm before paying. 

 License Cycle When the board writes to you On-time fee, and late After expiry 

 California contractor (CSLB) Active: every 2 years. Inactive: every 4 Renewal application sent about 60 days before expiry. Order one if it has not arrived 45 days before Sole owner, active: $450 on time, $675 delinquent. Other entities: $700, then $1,050 Work while expired is unlicensed. Renewable for 5 years, then a new application 

 Texas electrical contractor (TDLR) Not stated on the renewal page; read the date on your license Written notice at least 30 days before expiry, by law $110 on time. $165 if expired 90 days or less. $220 after that No licensed work until renewed. Over 18 months needs the executive director's approval. Over 36 months: apply as new 

 Washington contractor registration (L&I) 2 years A renewal card by mail; L&I's page does not say how far ahead $150.20 to renew. $70.90 to reinstate after a suspension Suspended if the bond or insurance cancels or expires; L&I notifies by certified mail within 2 days 

 Oregon residential contractor (CCB) 2 years Not stated on the page we read Not stated on the page we read Lapsed or expired more than 2 years: re-apply, with pre-license training and the test 

Sources: CSLB, General renewal information ; TDLR, Renew an electrical contractor license and Texas Occupations Code §51.401 ; Washington L&I, Register as a contractor and RCW 18.27.060 ; Oregon CCB, Continuing education . We tried to read Arizona's and Tennessee's board pages today and could not load them, so they are not in the table. 

## What a late renewal costs, worked out

The late fee is the small part. In California a sole owner pays $675 instead of $450, which is $225 more. A Texas electrical contractor pays $165 instead of $110 in the first 90 days, $55 more, and $220 after that, double. Texas sets those multiples in law: 1½ times the fee up to 90 days, twice the fee after (Occupations Code §51.401). 

The larger cost is the gap. The CSLB says that when you renew late "there will be a break in licensing time and any work performed while the license is expired is considered to be unlicensed". Texas law says a person whose license has expired "may not engage in activities that require a license until the license has been renewed". California has one cushion: since 2021 the registrar must retroactively reinstate an expired license if a completed renewal and the fees arrive within 90 days of expiry. The delinquent fee still applies, and an incomplete form does not count, so it is a backstop, not a plan. What an expired license does to contracts and insurance is covered in what happens if a business license expires . 

## The license date is not the only date

A renewal can be refused, or a current license suspended, because of something else that ran out. Each of these needs its own reminder. 

 The bond. In Washington a registration "shall be automatically suspended on the effective date" of a bond cancellation (RCW 18.27.060). Washington bonds are $30,000 for general and $15,000 for specialty contractors. 

 Liability insurance. Washington asks for a certificate of at least $250,000. Texas electrical contractors must hold $300,000 per occurrence and $600,000 aggregate, and the business name on the certificate must match the application. 

 Workers' compensation. An active California license must keep its bonds, workers' compensation cover and qualifying individual in place; the CSLB excuses only a license renewed as inactive. 

 Your qualifier. A Texas electrical contractor must employ a licensed master electrician or hold that license. If that person leaves, you must tell TDLR and name another. Their own license has its own expiry. 

 The company's standing. The CSLB checks a corporation's status with the Secretary of State before renewing and will not renew one that is suspended there. 

 Continuing education. Oregon residential contractors "cannot renew a license until the CCB has proof they met the continuing education requirements": 3 hours of laws and business practices plus 5 or 13 further hours each two-year period, depending on years licensed. 

 Your address. Notices go to the last address on record. Texas law says so in terms; the CSLB asks you to report any change. 

## A five-reminder plan built on the board's own dates

Count back from the expiry date printed on your license or pocket card. 

 The 60- and 45-day lines follow the CSLB's mailing dates; in another state, move them to match your board's notice. 

 Reminder What to do that day 

 90 days before Look yourself up on the board's license search. Check the address, the bond, the insurance and workers' comp certificates on file, and any education hours still owed. Book the classes now. 

 60 days before The board's form or notice should be arriving. Check the mail and the email address the board holds. 

 45 days before Nothing arrived? Order the renewal or log in to the board's portal. Not receiving a form does not excuse you: "It is your responsibility to make sure your license is renewed" (CSLB). 

 30 days before Submit and pay. The CSLB says processing times "can vary significantly". Keep the receipt. 

 7 days before Look the license up again ( how to read the lookup ). If the new expiry date is not showing, call the board that day. 

Then add one reminder 30 days before the bond's renewal date and one 30 days before each insurance policy's. Those dates rarely match the license date. The renewal steps themselves, form by form, are in how to renew a business license . 

## Worked example: a California sole owner whose license expires 31 March 2027

 Date Days before Action 

 31 December 2026 90 License check: address, bond, workers' comp certificate 

 30 January 2027 60 Renewal application due in the mail 

 14 February 2027 45 Not here? Order one online or on 1-800-321-2752 

 1 March 2027 30 Submit with the $450 fee 

 24 March 2027 7 Confirm the new date on the CSLB license check 

 31 March 2027 0 Expiry. A renewal received after today costs $675 

 29 June 2027 90 after Last day for a completed renewal to be reinstated retroactively 

### Renewal card to print and keep with the license

License number and class: ______________ Expires: ___ / ___ / ______ 

Board renewal page and phone: ______________________________ 

Board notice normally arrives ____ days before expiry 

On-time fee $______ Late fee $______ 

Bond: surety ____________ renews ___ / ___ / ______ 

Liability policy renews ___ / ___ / ______ Workers' comp renews ___ / ___ / ______ 

Qualifier or master of record: ____________ their license expires ___ / ___ / ______ 

Education hours owed: ____ done: ____ 

Reminders set at 90, 60, 45, 30 and 7 days, plus bond and insurance 

## Where to keep the reminders

A paper diary or a phone calendar works if you enter all five dates and create the next cycle's events the day you renew. A two-year gap is where a single calendar entry gets lost. Obligio, our app for iPhone and Android, is one option: it reminds you 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before each date you enter, and with Plus a recurring obligation rolls forward and you can attach the certificate. Its reminders start at 30 days, so for the 90- and 60-day checks enter the submit-by date as the due date. The free plan holds three obligations, which covers one license, one bond and one policy. It files nothing with any board and does not know your state's rules. 

## When this page does not apply

 Your license has already expired. Stop taking licensed work and call the board. Then read what happens if a business license expires . 

 Your state or trade is not in the table. Use your board's own renewal page. The reminder plan still works; change the 60- and 45-day lines to match its notice. 

 The business changed structure or owner. In California a change from sole owner to corporation means a new license, not a renewal. Ask the board before the renewal date. 

 You hold a city or county business license as well. That is a separate renewal; see the business license renewal tracker . 

 A discipline, suspension or criminal-history question is involved. Ask the board or a licensing attorney. 

## Questions

 How long before it expires can I renew a contractor license? 
It depends on the board. California's CSLB sends the renewal application about 60 days before expiry and says a renewal must be received before the expiration date to avoid unlicensed time. Texas law requires the licensing department to send written notice at least 30 days before expiry. Check your own board's renewal page for its window. 
 Can I keep working while my contractor license renewal is late? 
Generally no. The CSLB says work performed while a license is expired is considered unlicensed. Texas Occupations Code section 51.401 says a person whose license has expired may not engage in activities that require a license until it is renewed. Ask your board before taking or continuing a job. 
 What besides the license itself can stop me working? 
A cancelled bond or insurance policy. Washington law suspends a contractor's registration automatically on the date the bond is cancelled, and Washington's Department of Labor and Industries says it suspends a registration when a bond or insurance cancels or expires. Track those dates alongside the license date.

 Revised Code of Washington 18.27.060, Certificate of registration 

 Oregon Construction Contractors Board, Continuing education

How to Check if a Business License Is Valid | Obligio 

 Skip to content 

GUIDE 

# How to check if a business license is valid, and what to read on the result

To check if a business license is valid, look it up on the public search of the agency that issued it, not a third-party site: the state board for a trade or profession, the state revenue or licensing department for a general state license, and the city or county clerk for a local license. A valid license shows a status such as "Active" or "Current, Active", an expiry date after the work will finish, the right name and, for trades, the right classification. A Secretary of State "Active" entry is not a license at all; it only means the company exists. The tables below show which lookup answers which question, what each status word means, and five checks to make beyond the status line. Sources were read on 19 November 2026. 

## Which lookup answers which question

A business can hold several licenses from different agencies, and each agency only shows its own. Decide first which one you need to see. 

 Examples are from agencies whose pages we read today. Your state's equivalents will have different names. 

 You want to know Look it up at Examples 

 Is this contractor or professional licensed for this work? The state licensing board for that trade or profession California: CSLB Check a License (or 1-800-321-2752). Texas: TDLR Search / Verify Licenses . Washington: L&I Verify a contractor . Florida: DBPR's portal at myfloridalicense.com 

 Does the company legally exist? The Secretary of State's business entity search California's bizfile. This shows registration, not a license 

 Does it hold a general state business license? The state revenue or licensing department, where one exists Washington's Department of Revenue Business Lookup; its Business Licensing Service also issues endorsements for more than 200 cities and towns 

 Does it hold a city or county license? The city or county that issues it Many have no public search. Call or email the clerk or finance office with the business name and address 

The SBA puts the local part plainly: "Local governments determine registration, licensing, and permitting requirements" ( SBA, Apply for licenses and permits ). 

## Why "Active" at the Secretary of State is not enough

California's Secretary of State defines Active as an entity that "has filed its formation document in California and is authorized to carry out its business activities", and adds "subject to any other requirements imposed by law". The licenses are those other requirements. A company can be Active there and hold no contractor license, or an expired one. The reverse also matters: an entity shown as Suspended (by the Secretary of State for missing filings, or by the Franchise Tax Board for tax reasons) has lost its powers to do business in the state, and the CSLB will not renew a contractor license for a corporation that is suspended. Check both records when you are hiring a company rather than a person. 

## What the status words mean

Each agency uses its own words. Florida's Department of Business and Professional Regulation publishes a glossary, and its definitions are a clear guide to the common ones. 

 Definitions quoted from the DBPR licensing portal glossary , read 19 November 2026. Another state may use the same word differently; read its own help page. 

 Status Florida's definition Can they do the licensed work? 

 Current "up to date with respect to the department's requirements" Only if also Active 

 Active "allowed to operate under the associated license" Yes 

 Inactive has met the requirements "but is not allowed to work under this license" No 

 Delinquent "has not completed a timely renewal" No 

 Renewal in process filed for renewal on time and may keep operating until a decision Yes, for now 

 Suspended "work privileges have been suspended for a specified period" No 

 Probation placed on probation "as part of a disciplinary action" Depends on the terms of the order; ask the board 

 Revoked, Null and void, Vol. relinquish no longer meets the requirements; failed to renew several times; returned the license No 

California's CSLB writes its status as a sentence. An expired record reads "This license is expired and not able to contract at this time", and a second "Additional Status" line can say what is still needed, such as workers' compensation, before it can renew. 

## Five checks beyond the status line

A contractor's record answers more than "valid or not". Before you sign, check these in order and stop at the first one that fails. 

 Same business. The name and license number on the quote or truck match the record. If the company name differs, ask why. If they will not give a number, do not go further. 

 Right work. The classification covers the job. The CSLB tells consumers to confirm the contractor "is licensed for the specific type of work". A general building license is not an electrical or roofing one in every state. 

 Still valid when the job ends. The expiry date falls after your finish date. If it falls during the job, ask whether the renewal is in. 

 Bond and insurance on file. CSLB's detail page lists the contractor's bond (surety, number, amount, effective date) and the workers' compensation insurer and policy dates, or an exemption. Washington's Verify tool shows whether there are lawsuits against the bond and whether the workers' comp account is active and paid up. 

 History. Read the complaint, citation or violation section. It is incomplete by design: CSLB says its "complaint disclosure is restricted by law", only construction-related civil judgments reported to it are shown, and citations are shown for five years from compliance. 

Two cautions on the data itself. The CSLB says "there may be relevant information that has not yet been entered" because of workload, and Washington L&I says its database is updated on weekdays and "portions may be incorrect or not current". For a large job, print or save the page with the date, and call the board if anything looks wrong. 

## Worked example: hiring for an $8,000 bathroom remodel in California

The figures below are invented to show the reading; the rules are CSLB's. 

 Check What the record shows Verdict 

 Is a license needed? $8,000 job, with plumbing changes Yes. Above $1,000, and plumbing work is outside the minor-work exemption at any price 

 Same business License number on the quote matches; business name matches Pass 

 Status Shown as current and active Pass 

 Classification B, General Building Pass for a job needing two or more unrelated trades ( CSLB, B classification ); ask who does the plumbing 

 Expiry 31 January 2027; job runs December to January Pass, but close: ask about the renewal 

 Workers' comp Exempt (no employees) Ask who will be on site. If they bring a crew, the exemption does not fit 

California's minor-work threshold rose from $500 to $1,000 on 1 January 2025 under AB 2622. It does not apply to work that needs a permit, to plumbing, electrical, mechanical or structural changes, or when the unlicensed person employs anyone ( CSLB industry bulletin on AB 2622 ). Some older pages still say $500. 

## Checking your own license after you renew

If the license is yours, the public record is how a customer, a general contractor or a permit counter will see you. Look yourself up about a week after you pay. Check that the expiry date has moved forward, the address is current, and the bond and insurance shown are the policies you hold now. If the old date still shows, call the board that day; "renewal in process" is a status you want to see, not assume. The renewal steps are in how to renew a business license , and the dates to set reminders for are in contractor license renewal dates and reminders . 

### License check record: print one per contractor or license

Business name on the quote: ______________ License number: ______________ 

Agency and lookup used: ______________ Date checked: ___ / ___ / ______ 

Status as shown: ______________ Expires: ___ / ___ / ______ 

Classification shown: ______________ Covers this job: yes / no 

Bond: surety ______________ amount $______ 

Workers' comp: insurer ______________ or exempt; crew on site: yes / no 

Liability insurance certificate seen, expires: ___ / ___ / ______ 

Complaints, citations or bond claims shown: ______________ 

Entity status at the Secretary of State (companies): ______________ 

City or county license confirmed with: ______________ 

## Keeping the result

For a one-off hire the printed record is enough. For your own licenses, the useful habit is to look them up again before each renewal date. Obligio, our app for iPhone and Android, can hold those dates: it reminds you 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before each one, and with Plus you can attach the saved record or certificate. It does not look anything up or connect to any board; the check itself is the one on this page. 

## When this page does not apply

 You think someone is working unlicensed. Report it to the board that would license the work; most boards have a complaint form on the same site as the lookup. 

 Your own license has already expired. Stop licensed work and read what happens if a business license expires . 

 The license is outside the US. Use the issuing regulator's register. For an Australian company's registration, see the ASIC annual review date guide . 

 A contract dispute or a claim against a bond is already under way. Talk to the board and to a lawyer; the lookup only tells you where the bond is held. 

## Questions

 Is a business license number on an invoice proof that it is valid? 
No. A number can be old, belong to someone else or cover different work. Enter it on the issuing agency's own lookup and check the name, status, expiry date and classification shown there. 
 Does an active listing with the Secretary of State mean a business is licensed? 
No. California's Secretary of State defines Active as an entity that has filed its formation document and is authorized to carry out business activities, subject to any other requirements imposed by law. Licenses come from licensing boards and local governments and are looked up separately. 
 What if the license shows as delinquent or expired? 
The holder should not be doing the licensed work. Florida's DBPR defines delinquent as not having completed a timely renewal, and California's CSLB shows an expired license as not able to contract. Ask the holder for proof of renewal and recheck the lookup, or call the board.

How to Renew a Business License: Steps and Checklist | Obligio 

 Skip to content 

GUIDE 

# How to renew a business license: the six steps, and what to have ready

To renew a business license, find the agency named on the license, renew through that agency's own portal (or by mail or in person) inside its renewal window, and send everything the renewal asks for besides the fee: updated details, signatures, and any certificate it needs, such as proof of workers' compensation. Then check that the status has changed to current and file the new certificate. Every license renews separately with the agency that issued it, so a city license, a state license and a trade board license are three renewals, not one. Below are the six steps, what each agency in the examples actually asks for, a rule for how early to start, and a checklist to print. The examples are American; Australians spell it licence, and the ASIC annual review guide covers Australian companies. 

## Step 1: Find out who issued each license

The issuing agency's name is printed on the license. Write it down for each one, because there is rarely a single place that renews everything. The SBA says you "may also need licenses from your county or city" as well as the state, and that "you'll have to research your own state, county, and city regulations" ( SBA, Apply for licenses and permits ). New York's state portal says the same about renewals: many licenses "can be renewed online through the issuing agency's website" ( NY Business Express ). 

 What it is Usually issued by Example, read today 

 City or county business license (often a tax on gross receipts) The city or county finance or licensing office City of Columbia, South Carolina: "All Business Licenses expire on April 30th" ( Columbia Business License Division ). 

 State business license with endorsements The state revenue department Washington: a license with state or city endorsements through the Business Licensing Service is renewed annually ( WA Department of Revenue ). 

 Trade or professional license A state licensing board California contractors: "Active licenses expire every two years" ( CSLB, General renewal information ). 

If you are not sure what you hold, the business license renewal tracker lists what commonly expires and how often, with each agency's page linked. 

## Step 2: Find the window and the deadline

Two dates matter: the first day the agency will accept the renewal, and the expiry date. They differ by agency: 

 Washington: "You are eligible to renew your Business License up to two months before the expiration date printed on your license." Renewals received after that date are charged a late penalty ( WA DOR ). 

 California contractors: the board sends a renewal application about 60 days before expiry. If it has not arrived 45 days before, order one online or on 1-800-321-2752 ( CSLB ). 

 Columbia, SC: one date for every license, April 30. Renewal forms are mailed at the start of the year. After April 30 a 5% penalty is added, and another 5% on the first of each month until paid ( Columbia ). 

Not getting the notice does not move the date. Columbia's page says "failure to receive notice shall not constitute a defense", and New York's says that you may be reminded "but you are responsible for staying in compliance." 

## Step 3: Gather what the renewal asks for besides the fee

This is the step that causes late renewals. The fee takes a minute; a missing certificate or signature can take weeks. What the example agencies ask for: 

 Your login and license number. NY Business Express notes that "some agencies require you to set up an online account for renewals". Set it up before the window opens, not on the last day. 

 Current details. Address, owners and officers. The CSLB asks for the new address if it changed, and a street address if you use a PO box. Columbia requires a name or address change to be reported within ten days, not at renewal. 

 Proof of insurance or an exemption. A California contractor with employees attaches a current certificate of workers' compensation insurance; one without employees certifies they "continue to have no employees". Without it, "the license will not be renewed" ( CSLB, Completing your renewal application ). 

 Every required signature. For a California contractor that means the owner, or all general partners, or the listed officers, and every qualifier (same page). 

 Re-validation forms. In Columbia, a home occupation or mobile food business resubmits its home occupation form or food service questionnaire with the renewal, so zoning can check it again. 

 Continuing education, a bond or an inspection , where the license requires them. Check your agency's renewal page for these words. 

## Step 4: Submit it, by the route that is fastest for you

Online is usually quickest. Columbia gives its own processing times: portal renewals up to 3 to 5 days, in person immediate, mail 10 business days, and up to 8 weeks for mail in the February to May peak. Card payments in its portal carry a 2.90% fee and ACH $1.25. Washington takes renewals online through My DOR or by a paper form requested on 360-705-6705, and recommends mailing early "as postmarks may take a few days". The CSLB accepts a personal, certified or cashier's check or money order, never cash. Its timely active renewal fee is $450 for a sole owner and $700 for other owners. After expiry those become $675 and $1,050 ( CSLB fees ). 

## Step 5: Confirm it went through

Paying is not the same as being renewed. The CSLB warns that "incomplete applications will be returned for corrections and may result in a period of unlicensed time." A week after submitting, look up the license on the agency's public lookup (Washington's Business Lookup, CSLB License Check) and check the new expiry date. Save a screenshot. When the certificate arrives, store it, and post it if your license must be displayed: Washington notes that some licenses must be posted before you open to the public. 

## Step 6: Set the next renewal before you close the file

You will never know the next date better than today. Add it to your calendar or tracker with three reminders: the day the window opens, 30 days before expiry and 7 days before. The renewal tracker guide explains the reasoning and has a template to copy. 

## How early to start: a rule

 The renewal is a fee and a form in a portal you can log into: start when the window opens, or 30 days before expiry if there is no window. 

 It needs something from someone else (an insurance certificate, a bond, continuing education hours, a signature from a partner or officer, an inspection): start 90 days before expiry, because you are waiting on them. 

 You are renewing by mail, or the agency renews everyone on one date (like Columbia's April 30): start as soon as the form arrives. Peak-season mail took up to 8 weeks there. 

## The renewal checklist (print it)

One copy per license. 

☐ License: ______________ Number: __________ Agency: ______________ 

☐ Window opens: ___/___/___ Expires: ___/___/___ Late fee or penalty: $______ 

☐ Portal login works (tested on ___/___/___) 

☐ Address, owners and officers on file are current 

☐ Insurance or workers' compensation certificate, or exemption, ready 

☐ Bond, continuing education or inspection done, if required 

☐ Every required person has signed 

☐ Any re-validation form (zoning, home occupation) attached 

☐ Fee paid on ___/___/___ by ______ Receipt saved 

☐ Status checked on the agency lookup: current, new expiry ___/___/___ 

☐ New certificate stored (and posted, if required) 

☐ Next window and expiry entered with three reminders 

## Where Obligio fits

Obligio is a compliance tracker for iPhone and Android. Enter a license with its expiry date and it reminds you 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before, with notifications enabled. With Plus, you can attach the certificate to the license, and a recurring obligation rolls forward to the next date when you mark it complete. That covers steps 5 and 6. It does not renew anything, find your agency or know your requirements; you enter those yourself. The free plan tracks three obligations. The checklist above works without it. 

## When this page does not apply

 The license has already expired. The consequences and the fix-it order are in what happens if a business license expires . Renew today if the portal lets you. 

 You sold the business or changed its structure. A renewal may not be the right form. Columbia, for example, says a license "shall not be transferable" and a change of ownership needs a new license. Ask the agency. 

 You need to know which licenses you need at all. Use your state's business portal or licensing wizard (Washington's Business Licensing Wizard, New York's Business Wizard), or the SBA's local assistance. 

 It is a tax filing or annual report rather than a license. See the small business compliance calendar . 

 Your case turns on a notice from the agency or a legal question. Phone the agency, or ask a licensed attorney or accountant. This page is organizational guidance, not legal or tax advice. 

 You hold a state contractor license. Board cycles, late fees and a reminder plan that covers the bond and insurance are in contractor license renewal dates and reminders . 

## Questions

 How do I renew my business license online? 
Go to the website of the agency printed on the license, not a third-party site, log in to its portal (set up the account first if it asks for one), find the renewal in your account, update your details, attach any certificate it asks for, and pay. Washington renews through My DOR; Columbia, South Carolina, through its self-service portal or the statewide renewal portal. Then check the license lookup a week later to confirm the new expiry date. How early can I renew a business license? 
It depends on the agency. Washington accepts a renewal up to two months before the printed expiry date. The California Contractors State License Board mails the renewal application about 60 days before expiry. Columbia, South Carolina, renews every license on one date, April 30, and mails forms at the start of the year. If your agency does not say, start 30 days before expiry, or 90 days if the renewal needs an insurance certificate, bond, training or someone else's signature. Do I renew city, county and state licenses separately? 
Usually, yes. Each license renews with the agency that issued it. The SBA says you may need licenses from your county or city as well as the state. Some states bundle city endorsements into one renewal: Washington's Business Licensing Service renews state and city endorsements together on one license. Check whether each of yours is covered by a bundle before assuming it is. What if I did not get a renewal notice? 
Renew anyway; the date on the license is the deadline. Columbia, South Carolina, says failure to receive notice is no defense and does not waive penalties. The California Contractors State License Board asks you to order a renewal application if it has not arrived 45 days before expiry. Update your mailing address with the agency at the same time.

 City of Columbia, SC, Business license renewal 

 California Contractors State License Board, General renewal information 

 California Contractors State License Board, Completing your renewal application 

All sources were read on 12 November 2026. Fees and dates change; confirm them on your own agency's page or notice. 

If you want the next renewal date on your phone, Obligio is free for your first three obligations: download on the App Store or get it on Google Play . Questions about the app go to support .

License Renewal Reminder Calendar in Google Calendar | Obligio 

 Skip to content

# License renewal reminders in Google Calendar: the setup that works, where it stops, and when a tracker fits better

Google Calendar works as a license renewal reminder calendar if you give each license two events, not one. The first is an all-day event on the expiry date, repeating on the license's cycle (every year, every two years), with reminders 4 weeks, 2 weeks, 1 week and 1 day before. The second is a "start the renewal" event 60 to 90 days earlier, because Google allows no reminder more than 4 weeks before an event and no more than five per event. That is enough for a handful of licenses. A calendar does not know whether you renewed. The event repeats either way, and a missed date simply scrolls into the past. Once you hold more than about five dated items, or need the certificate kept beside the date, a tracker does that job better. 

## Set it up in Google Calendar: two events per license

These steps use Google Calendar on a computer, following Google's own help pages for recurring events and notifications . 

### Event 1: the expiry date

Click Create . Title it with the license and number, for example "CSLB license 1234567 expires". 

Tick All day and set the date to the expiry date printed on the license. 

Next to "Does not repeat", open the menu and choose the license's cycle. For a two-year license, choose Custom and set it to repeat every 2 years. 

Under notifications, click Add notification until you have four: 4 weeks, 2 weeks, 1 week and 1 day before, each at a time you will be at work. 

In the description, paste the board's renewal page link and the license number. Click Save . 

### Event 2: start the renewal

Create a second all-day event 60 to 90 days before the expiry date, titled "Start renewal: CSLB 1234567". 

Repeat it on the same cycle as event 1. 

Give it a reminder 1 day before, and list in the description what the renewal needs: fee, continuing education, bond, insurance certificate. 

Ninety days is the start we suggest in our contractor license renewal guide , because continuing-education hours and insurance certificates take weeks to arrange. If your board only needs a fee, 60 days is enough. 

## Worked example: a California contractor license expiring 31 January 2027

The California Contractors State License Board (CSLB) renews an active license every two years and sends the renewal application about 60 days before expiry; if none has arrived 45 days before, you can order one ( CSLB, General renewal information ). Here is how each reminder you would want maps onto Google Calendar: 

 Reminders for an expiry date of 31 January 2027, counted in calendar days 

 Reminder Date Can it go on the expiry event? 

 90 days: start the renewal 2 November 2026 No: more than 4 weeks ahead. Use event 2 

 60 days: CSLB application should arrive 2 December 2026 No. Add a note to event 2: "order a form if none by 17 Dec" 

 4 weeks 3 January 2027 Yes, the earliest the event allows 

 2 weeks 17 January 2027 Yes 

 1 week 24 January 2027 Yes 

 1 day 30 January 2027 Yes (that is four of the five allowed) 

If you renew on 10 December 2026, nothing in the calendar changes. The reminders on 3, 17, 24 and 30 January still fire, and you dismiss them. That is harmless. The risk runs the other way: if you never renew, the calendar shows 31 January 2027 like any other past day, and the next event appears in 2029 as if all were well. 

## Where a calendar stops working

 Google Calendar limits for renewal reminders, and what to add if you need more 

 Need Google Calendar If you need it 

 Warning more than 4 weeks ahead Not on the event itself (maximum 40,320 minutes) A second "start" event 

 More than five reminders Five custom reminders per event Spread them across the two events 

 Knowing a renewal is overdue No status. A past event looks the same done or not done A tracker or spreadsheet with a status column 

 Next date only after you renew The series repeats regardless A tracker that opens the next cycle when you mark it done 

 Certificate kept with the date Up to 25 attachments per event, as Google Drive files Works if you already use Drive 

 A second person reminded Each person sets their own notifications, even on a shared calendar Ask them to set their own notifications on the shared calendar 

Limits from Google's Calendar API reference for events (reminders, attachments) and Change Google Calendar notifications (personal settings). We read them on 23 November 2026 and did not find the 4-week limit stated on Google's consumer help pages. 

## Calendar or tracker: a decision rule

 Up to about five licenses and policies, and you open your calendar every working day: use Google Calendar with the two-event setup. It costs nothing and you already look at it. 

 More than five, or dates on different cycles (annual insurance, two-year license, five-year permit): keep a list with a status column, either the spreadsheet set up this way or a tracker app. The calendar can still carry the expiry events. 

 Someone else needs to see what is overdue, or an inspector or general contractor asks for proof: use a tracker that keeps the document with the date. 

Obligio, our app for iPhone and Android, is one such tracker. It reminds you 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before each date, at 9 am. That schedule is fixed, so it cannot give a 90-day warning either; add a separate "start renewal" item for that. A date that passes without being marked done shows as overdue. With Plus, recurring items open their next cycle only when you mark the current one done, and you can attach the certificate. It does not sync to Google Calendar, does not share with a second person, and does not check any board. 

## If you import a calendar file instead

Our renewal reminder calculator makes a standard .ics calendar file with the reminders built in. After importing it into Google Calendar, open the event and check that the notifications are there. Google's import help page does not say whether imported reminders are kept, and we have not tested every account type. Add them by hand if they are missing. 

### Two-event setup card: one per license

License and number: ______________ Issued by: ______________ 

Expiry date on the license: ___ / ___ / ______ Cycle: 1 / 2 / 3 / 5 years 

Event 1 created on the expiry date, repeating on the cycle 

Reminders on event 1: 4 weeks, 2 weeks, 1 week, 1 day 

Start date (60 or 90 days before): ___ / ___ / ______ Event 2 created 

Renewal needs: fee $______ CE hours ______ bond / insurance certificate 

Board's renewal page pasted in both descriptions 

After renewing: new expiry date ___ / ___ / ______ matches the next event 

Bond and insurance have their own events (they expire on their own dates) 

## When this page does not apply

 The date has already passed. Stop licensed work and read what happens if a business license expires . 

 You need the state's annual report date, not a license. Find it in annual report due dates by state , then add it the same way. 

 You manage licenses for a team or several locations. Compare the options in compliance software for small business . 

 You do not know the renewal steps yet. Start with how to renew a business license . 

## Questions

 How far ahead can Google Calendar remind me about a license renewal? 
Google's Calendar API reference allows reminders between 0 and 40,320 minutes (4 weeks) before an event, and at most five custom reminders per event. For a 60- or 90-day warning, create a second event on that date called "Start the renewal" and give it its own reminders. 
 If I share the calendar with my bookkeeper, will they get my reminders? 
No. Google says notification settings are personal and apply only to your account, even for people you share the calendar with. Each person has to set their own notifications. 
 What should a repeating renewal event be based on: the expiry date or the day I renewed? 
The expiry date printed on the license. When the renewed license arrives, check that the next event in the series matches the new expiry date. If it does not, edit that event and choose "This and following events" so the rest of the series moves with it.

All sources were read on 23 November 2026. Google changes its products, and the issuing agency is the authority on your dates. This page is organizational guidance, not legal advice.

Small Business Compliance Calendar: Yearly Template & Dates | Obligio 

 Skip to content 

GUIDE 

# Small business compliance calendar: the dates that apply to you, and a yearly template

A small business compliance calendar is a month-by-month list of every filing, payment, posting and renewal your business owes in the coming year, with the rule behind each date so you can check it. For a United States business the federal rows are fixed and listed below with the agency's own wording; the state rows (annual report, sales tax, licenses) you add from your state's pages. The quickest way to build yours: answer the four questions in the next section to find out which rows apply to you, copy the yearly template, delete the rows that do not, and add your state dates. One thing older calendars still list and you can take off: the beneficial ownership (BOI) report, which U.S. companies no longer file (see the questions at the end). 

## Which rows apply to you: four questions

Most of a compliance calendar depends on four facts about the business. Decide them first, then the template nearly fills itself. 

 Entity type. Sole proprietor or single-member LLC: the business income goes on your Form 1040, due April 15. Partnership or multi-member LLC: Form 1065 by March 15. S corporation: Form 1120-S by March 15. C corporation: Form 1120 by April 15, with its own estimated tax dates (IRS Publication 509, Tax Calendars ). 

 Do you expect to owe $1,000 or more in tax (individuals, including sole proprietors, partners and S corporation shareholders) or $500 or more (corporations)? If so, the quarterly estimated tax rows apply (IRS, Estimated taxes ). 

 Do you have employees? If yes, the payroll rows apply: Form 941 each quarter, Form 940 and Forms W-2 in January, and your deposit schedule (IRS, Employment tax due dates ). If you paid any non-employee $2,000 or more during the year (the threshold rose from $600 for tax years beginning after 2025; IRS Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC ), Form 1099-NEC is due January 31 whether or not you have employees. 

 How many employees, at the most, during the year? More than 10 brings OSHA's injury and illness log and the posted annual summary, unless your industry is exempt (OSHA, Recordkeeping ). 20 or more in a listed industry, or 250 or more anywhere, adds an electronic submission ( 29 CFR 1904.41 ). 50 or more full-time or full-time-equivalent employees makes you an applicable large employer with Forms 1094-C and 1095-C (IRS, Information reporting by ALEs ). 

## The federal dates and the rule behind each

Each row gives the rule as the agency states it and the date it produces for a calendar-year business. The IRS moves a date that falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday to the next business day (Publication 509 gives the 2025 W-2 copies as due "by February 2, 2026", because January 31 was a Saturday). The PDF calendars in each year's Publication 509 already include that adjustment, so take next year's exact dates from the 2027 edition when it is published, usually in December. 

 What Who The rule, as the agency states it Date (calendar year) 

 Form 1099-NEC to contractors and the IRS Anyone who paid a non-employee $2,000 or more "Must be filed with the IRS and provided to recipients by Jan. 31" ( IRS ) Jan 31 

 Forms W-2 to employees, W-2 and W-3 to the SSA Employers "Forms W-2 are required to be provided to employees by Jan. 31" ( IRS ) Jan 31 

 Form 940, federal unemployment tax Employers Filed annually, due Jan. 31; ten extra days if all FUTA tax was deposited on time ( IRS ) Jan 31 

 Form 941, quarterly payroll return Employers "By the last day of the month that follows the end of the quarter"; ten extra days if the tax was deposited on time ( IRS ) Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, and Jan 31 for Q4 

 Payroll tax deposits Employers Monthly depositors: "by the 15th day of the following month". Semi-weekly depositors: Wednesday to Friday paydays by the following Wednesday, Saturday to Tuesday paydays by the following Friday ( IRS ) Recurring; the IRS sets your schedule from a lookback period 

 OSHA Form 300A posted in the workplace More than 10 employees, non-exempt industries "Post the summary no later than February 1 of the year following the year covered by the records and keep the posting in place until April 30"; a company executive certifies it ( 29 CFR 1904.32 ) Feb 1 to Apr 30 

 OSHA electronic submission (ITA) 20 to 249 employees in an appendix A industry, or 250 or more Submitted "once per year to OSHA from January 2 – March 2" ( OSHA ); part-time, seasonal and temporary workers each count as one employee ( 29 CFR 1904.41 ) Mar 2 

 Form 1065, partnership return, with Schedules K-1 Partnerships and multi-member LLCs taxed as partnerships "Due on the 15th day of the 3rd month after the end of the partnership's tax year"; Form 7004 gives a six-month extension ( Pub. 509 ) Mar 15 

 Form 1120-S, S corporation return, with Schedules K-1 S corporations "Due on the 15th day of the 3rd month after the end of the corporation's tax year"; Form 7004 gives a six-month extension ( Pub. 509 ) Mar 15 

 Form 1040 with Schedule C Sole proprietors and single-member LLCs "Due on the 15th day of the 4th month after the end of your tax year"; Form 4868 gives a six-month extension ( Pub. 509 ) Apr 15 

 Form 1120, C corporation return C corporations "Due on the 15th day of the 4th month after the end of the corporation's tax year"; Form 7004 gives a six-month extension ( Pub. 509 ) Apr 15 

 Individual estimated tax, four payments Owners expecting to owe $1,000 or more "Due on the 15th day of the 4th, 6th, and 9th months of your tax year" and the 1st month after it ends ( Pub. 509 ); on time if paid the next business day when the date is a weekend or holiday ( IRS ) Apr 15, Jun 15, Sep 15, Jan 15 of the next year 

 Corporate estimated tax, four payments C corporations expecting to owe $500 or more Four instalments, listed in the corporation calendar ( Pub. 509 ) Apr 15, Jun 15, Sep 15, Dec 15 

 Forms 1095-C to employees, 1094-C and 1095-C to the IRS Applicable large employers (50 or more full-time or equivalent) Furnish "by January 31 of the calendar year following the calendar year for which the information relates"; file "no later than February 28 (March 31 if filed electronically)" ( IRS ) Jan 31 furnish; Feb 28 or Mar 31 file 

 Form 1099-MISC and other information returns Payers of rent, prizes, other reportable amounts Recipient copies by Jan. 31; filed "by the last day of February, or by March 31 if filed electronically" ( IRS ) Jan 31; Feb 28 or Mar 31 

Every employer, whatever its size, must also report a work-related death to OSHA within 8 hours and an in-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye within 24 hours ( OSHA ). That is an event, not a date, but it belongs on the same sheet so it is not forgotten. 

## The yearly template (copy it)

Select the table and paste it into a spreadsheet or document. Rows marked "state" are placeholders for you to fill from your state's revenue department and Secretary of State pages; dates in those rows are deliberately blank. Delete the rows the four questions ruled out. The reminder column follows the rule in the next section. 

 Small business compliance calendar template. Federal rows carry the agency's rule; state rows are yours to fill in.

Print it with the browser's print command: the header and footer are hidden on paper. The reminder dates in the template follow the 30, 14, 7 and 1 day rule below, counted back from the rule date, and are not adjusted for weekends. 

## How far ahead to set each reminder

A single reminder on the day is too late for anything that needs a document, a login or a payment. Use four, counted back from the due date: 30 days (gather the figures, find the portal login), 14 days (prepare or hand to your accountant), 7 days (file or pay if ready), 1 day (confirm it went through and store the confirmation). For a renewal whose window opens earlier than 30 days out, the business license renewal tracker page explains why the first reminder should land the day the window opens. 

## What goes in the state rows

Federal dates are the same everywhere; state dates are not, which is why the template leaves them blank rather than guessing. The rows most small businesses need are the annual report or statement of information, a franchise or privilege tax, sales tax returns on a monthly, quarterly or annual cycle set by the state, the state unemployment insurance return, workers' compensation renewal, and business license renewals. Verified examples with the agencies' own pages, including Delaware's March 1 franchise tax, Texas's May 15 report, Oregon's anniversary-date renewal and California's six-month statement window, are on the renewal tracker page . For which licenses your business must hold at all, start with your Secretary of State and the SBA's licenses and permits guide . 

## Where Obligio fits

 Obligio is a compliance tracker for iPhone and Android that holds the same rows as the template, each with its due date, category and the same four reminders (30, 14, 7 and 1 days before, at 9 am local time, with notifications enabled), and shows what is current, upcoming and overdue in a dashboard and calendar ( features ). The Free plan tracks three obligations, enough for a sole proprietor's estimated tax, state sales tax and one license. Plus adds unlimited obligations, recurring ones that roll forward when you mark them complete (monthly, quarterly or annual, which fits the 941 and estimated tax rows), and attached documents so the filed return sits with its deadline ( Free and Plus ). It does not tell you which rows apply to your business, file anything, or give tax advice; the questions and template above do the deciding, and they work without it. 

## When this page does not apply

If your business has a fiscal year that is not the calendar year, the return and estimated tax dates shift with it; Publication 509 gives the month-based rules. 

If you are outside the United States, the federal rows do not apply. Australian businesses have the ATO's key dates for employers ; the template still works with those dates in it. 

If you have already missed a date, go to the agency's own page for penalties and late filing rather than this calendar. 

Anything that turns on your entity election, your industry's exemption status under OSHA appendix A, or a notice an agency sent you is a question for a CPA, an enrolled agent or an attorney. This page is organizational guidance, not tax or legal advice. 

## Questions

 Do I still need to file a beneficial ownership (BOI) report? 
Not if your company was formed in the United States. FinCEN's interim final rule of March 26, 2025 exempted domestic reporting companies, and a final rule issued August 11, 2026 and effective August 14, 2026 made the exemption permanent ( FinCEN, Beneficial Ownership Information ). Older compliance calendars still list it; take it off yours. 
 What if a deadline falls on a weekend or holiday? 
For federal tax deadlines the IRS says the action is on time if done by the next day that is not a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday ( Pub. 509 ). Its PDF calendars already reflect that: the 2026 edition gives the W-2 copies for 2025 as due February 2, 2026. Copy next year's dates from the 2027 edition when it is published. 
 Which OSHA dates apply to a small business? 
With more than 10 employees in a non-exempt industry, you keep the 300 log and post the Form 300A summary from February 1 to April 30 ( 29 CFR 1904.32 ). Electronic submission by March 2 applies only to establishments with 20 to 249 employees in an appendix A industry, or 250 or more employees ( 29 CFR 1904.41 ). Every employer must report a death within 8 hours and a hospitalization, amputation or eye loss within 24 hours ( OSHA ). 
 Where do state deadlines go? 
As rows under the month they fall in. The usual ones are the annual report, franchise tax, sales tax returns, the state unemployment return and license renewals; the renewal tracker page has verified examples and the columns to record for each.

Business License Expired? What Happens and What to Do | Obligio 

 Skip to content 

GUIDE 

# What happens if a business license expires, and what to do today

When a business license expires, three things usually follow, in this order. First, the renewal gets more expensive: a late or delinquent fee is added the day after the printed date (Washington, California's cosmetology board) or a penalty plus monthly interest starts (Delaware, Texas). Second, if the license is the permission to do the work, the work you do while it is expired counts as unlicensed, and the agency can discipline you for it. Third, after a cutoff, which runs from 45 days to five years depending on the agency, you can no longer renew at all: the license is cancelled or the entity forfeited, and you reapply or reinstate from scratch. Renew today if the portal still lets you, and read your agency's own rule in the table below. The examples are American; Australians spell it licence, and the address keeps that spelling so both can find this page. 

## The three consequences, with the agencies' own rules

Each row below was read on the agency's page on the day this was written and links to it. Your license is governed by its own agency, so use these to know what to look for, then find the matching sentence on your agency's site. 

 License or filing Day after expiry While it stays expired The cutoff 

 Washington state business license (Department of Revenue) "Renewals are due by the expiration date. Renewals received after the expiration date are charged a late penalty fee" ( WA DOR FAQs ). The reminder arrives one month before expiry; the due date stands whether or not it reaches you. The late penalty applies to the renewal. The FAQ page does not describe a further step, so ask the Business Licensing Service (360-705-6705 on the same page) if yours has lapsed for long. Not stated on the FAQ page; ask. 

 California barber, cosmetologist or salon establishment license (Board of Barbering and Cosmetology) The status changes from Current to Delinquent, "license holder has not complied with renewal requirements", and a delinquent fee is added: $25 on a $50 individual renewal, $20 on a $40 establishment renewal ( Board of Barbering and Cosmetology ). The license stays Delinquent until the renewal and delinquent fee are paid. "Canceled – license holder did not comply with renewal requirements for 5 years" (same page). 

 California contractor license (Contractors State License Board) "You will be required to pay the delinquent renewal fee." A written petition for retroactive renewal is possible only if "the CSLB must receive a written petition within 90 days of the expiration date", and a granted petition still carries the delinquent fee ( CSLB, Failing to renew your license ). "Any work performed while the license is expired is considered to be unlicensed" and "disciplinary action can be taken against you" (same page). "You may renew an expired license any time within five years after its expiration." After that, "you will be required to reapply by completing an Application for Original License" (same page). 

 Delaware corporation annual report and franchise tax (Division of Corporations) Due on or before March 1. "Failure to file the report and pay the required franchise taxes will result in a penalty of $200.00 plus 1.5% interest per month on tax and penalty" ( Delaware Division of Corporations ). The interest compounds monthly on tax and penalty until paid. Not on the page read; the Division's help center covers void and revived status. 

 Texas franchise tax report (Comptroller of Public Accounts) "A $50 penalty is assessed on each report filed after the due date", plus a percentage penalty on tax paid late ( Texas Comptroller, Franchise tax ). A Notice of Intent to Forfeit Right to Transact Business (Form 05-211) follows. The Comptroller must "give at least 45 days, beginning after the notice of pending forfeiture is mailed", and "any franchise tax deficiencies must be cured during that period" ( Texas Comptroller, Franchise tax account status ). After forfeiture the entity "will be denied the right to sue or defend itself in a Texas court" and "each director or officer will be liable for the debt of the entity" (same page). Reinstatement is possible "at any time (so long as the entity would otherwise continue to exist)" by filing the missing reports, paying tax, penalties and interest, and filing an application on SOSDirect "accompanied by a tax clearance letter (form 05-377)" ( Texas Secretary of State, Terminations and reinstatements FAQs ). 

 California Statement of Information (Secretary of State) A missed statutory filing "may result in penalties being assessed by the Franchise Tax Board" ( California Secretary of State ). Penalties accrue with the Franchise Tax Board. "Suspension or forfeiture" (same page). 

 EPA lead-safe (RRP) firm certification Certifications "are good for five years"; a re-certification application is due at least 90 days before expiry ( EPA ). A firm whose certification has lapsed may not conduct renovations until EPA approves a new application (same page). The firm "can submit a new application for certification, along with the correct amount of fees, at any time" (same page). 

## Can you keep working? A rule to apply in the first ten minutes

Sort your expired item into one of three kinds, because the right first move differs: 

 Permission to do the work (trade, professional, contractor, certification such as EPA lead-safe): stop that work until the renewal is accepted. The CSLB and EPA rules above are explicit that work in the gap is unlicensed or not permitted. Finish nothing on site today that the license covers. 

 Entity registration or tax filing (annual report, statement of information, franchise tax): the business keeps trading, but every day adds penalty or interest, and the real risk is the cutoff: forfeiture, suspension or a void entity. In Texas that means losing the right to sue or defend and personal liability for officers. File and pay within the notice period, today if the portal allows. 

 General business license or permit (state or city business license, sales tax permit, DBA): pay the renewal and late penalty now. Then read the agency's page for a second consequence; where the page is silent, as Washington's FAQ is, phone and write down what you were told, with the date and the name. 

If a renewal notice, a notice of intent to forfeit, or any letter with a deadline has arrived, that letter's date overrides everything above: it is the agency telling you how long you have. 

## What to do today, in order

 Find the document and the number. The license certificate, the policy, or the last filing confirmation. The expiry date printed on it is the one the agency works from. 

 Check the status on the agency's portal , not from memory. Boards publish the status (Current, Delinquent, Canceled); comptrollers publish account status. Save a screenshot with today's date. 

 Renew in the portal if it still lets you. Pay the delinquent or late fee with the renewal; it cannot be waived by asking, as the CSLB says even of a granted petition. 

 If the portal refuses the renewal , you are past the cutoff. Look for the words reapply, reinstate, original application or tax clearance letter on the agency's page, and start that process the same day. Keep every receipt. 

 If a petition or cure window exists, calendar its end date now. The CSLB's 90 days and Texas's 45 days are counted from the expiry date or the mailing of the notice, not from the day you noticed. 

 Record the lapse in the table below and attach the new certificate when it arrives. The record is what you show a client, an insurer or an auditor who asks about the gap. 

 Fix the cause. Most lapses have one of four causes: no reminder set, the reminder on a phone that was replaced, the agency's notice sent to an old address, or the person who renewed last time has left. Change the one that applies before you close the file. 

## The lapse record (copy it)

One row per expired item. It gives you the dates you will be asked for later and makes the cause of the lapse visible. The values shown are placeholders. 

 Lapse record. Example row only: replace every value with your own. 

 Obligation Agency and page Expired on Noticed on Kind (work / entity / general) Agency's rule, quoted Window ends Late fee or penalty paid Renewed or reinstated on Proof stored Cause and fix 

 Contractor license (example) State licensing board, renewals page 2026-09-30 2026-10-29 Work "Any work performed while the license is expired is considered to be unlicensed" 2026-12-29 (90-day petition) $ (delinquent fee) 2026-10-30 Compliance/Licenses/contractor-2026-renewal.pdf Notice went to the old office address; address updated in the portal 

 Franchise tax report (example) State comptroller 2026-05-15 2026-10-29 Entity "$50 penalty is assessed on each report filed after the due date" 45 days after a notice is mailed $50 + interest 2026-10-29 Compliance/Tax/franchise-2026.pdf No reminder existed; added to the tracker with three reminders 

Print it with the browser's print command; the header and footer are hidden on paper. Keep it with the renewal tracker , which is the list that stops the next lapse. 

## Stopping the next one

The agencies above send one reminder, late in the cycle, or none. So the fix is your own list with three reminder dates per item: when the renewal window opens, 30 days before expiry, and 7 days before. The business license renewal tracker page gives the template and the reasoning; the small business compliance calendar covers the federal filing dates that are not licenses at all. If you would rather hold the list on your phone, Obligio stores each obligation with its date and sends reminders 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before it, shows an item in red as overdue once the date has passed, and can attach the certificate as evidence on the Plus plan ( features ). It does not know your agency's rules, renew anything for you, or give legal advice; the table above is yours to keep either way. 

## When this page does not apply

 The license was suspended or revoked , not expired. That is a disciplinary matter with its own process (the cosmetology board lists Suspension and Revoked as separate statuses from Delinquent). Speak to the board and, for anything beyond a fee, a licensed attorney. 

 You received a notice with a deadline. Follow the notice. If it names a court, a hearing or personal liability, as a Texas forfeiture notice can, get an attorney or CPA involved before the window closes. 

 You are in Australia. The Australian Business Licence and Information Service lists licences by location and activity, and company annual review fees are set by ASIC (see our ASIC annual review date guide for the deadlines and late fees). The steps above still work; the examples do not. 

 It is an insurance policy, not a license. A lapsed policy is a gap in cover, and the insurer's reinstatement terms govern. Call the broker first; some will not backdate. 

 You are not sure which licenses you should hold. Start with your Secretary of State's site and the SBA's guide, which says to "research your own state, county, and city regulations" ( SBA ). This page is organizational guidance, not legal or tax advice. 

## Questions

 Is there a grace period after a business license expires? 
Only if the agency's own page says so, and the pages read for this one describe windows rather than grace periods. The CSLB accepts a written petition for retroactive renewal within 90 days of expiry, but the delinquent fee is still payable and work done in the gap is still unlicensed. Texas gives at least 45 days after a notice of pending forfeiture is mailed. Washington charges a late penalty on any renewal received after the expiration date. Treat a window as a deadline, not a cushion. 
 Can I keep operating while my business license is expired? 
If the license is the permission to do the work, assume no: the CSLB says work performed while expired is unlicensed, and the EPA says a lapsed lead-safe firm may not conduct renovations until re-approved. If it is a registration or tax filing, the business usually keeps trading while penalties grow, and the risk is forfeiture or suspension once the notice period passes. Read your own agency's wording before deciding. 
 Does renewing late or reinstating erase the gap? 
Not always. Texas lets a forfeited entity reinstate at any time with the missing reports, payment and a tax clearance letter (form 05-377), but the Comptroller's page says directors and officers are liable for the entity's debt during forfeiture. The CSLB lets you renew within five years, but the work in between was unlicensed. Keep the dates in the lapse record so you can answer the question later. 
 I never received a renewal reminder. Does that matter? 
Not to the agency. Washington sends a courtesy reminder one month before expiry and says the renewal is due by the expiration date whether or not the notice arrives; Oregon's Secretary of State sends its notice about 45 days ahead ( Oregon SOS ). The date on the document is the obligation. Fix the address on file when you renew, and keep your own reminders.
